about.edition.rms-preview.meaning: One-line description of the RMS editor preview edition.

about.disclosure.independent.preview.message: An independent, unofficial random map script editor. Its own implementation reproduces how Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition reads random map scripts and generates maps.
about.disclosure.independent.preview.meaning: Disclosure that the app is independent and unofficial. Keep the product name as written.

about.disclosure.verified-versions.message: Generated maps are only guaranteed to match the game for verified game versions; newer versions work without that guarantee. Some of the game's quirks are reproduced on purpose, so that maps behave the same.
about.disclosure.verified-versions.meaning: Reviewed disclosure: generated maps match the game only for verified game versions.

about.disclosure.game-files.textures.message: AoE2RMSIDE ships no game files and no game art. Official resources are only read from a local installation, and Game textures are only extracted from installed game files.
about.disclosure.game-files.textures.meaning: Reviewed disclosure about game data. Game textures is the name of a preview look.

about.disclosure.game-files.message: AoE2RMSIDE ships no game files and no game art. Official resources are only read from a local installation.

about.disclosure.affiliation.message: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft, Xbox Game Studios, World's Edge or Activision.

output.clear.meaning: Icon-only button beside the Output severity filter (its accessible name and tooltip): removes the messages and finished runs shown in Output.

output.source.run.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Runs of the preview (generating the map in the editor). Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.script.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Messages about the script itself, such as its syntax. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.preview.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: The live map preview. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.map-test.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Map tests (scripts that generate many maps and check them). Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.deploy.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Deploying a map as a local mod. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.live-test.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Live tests: starting the map in the running game through AoE2Control. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.recovery.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Restoring unsaved work after a restart. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.update.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Updates of the app. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.files.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: Opening, saving, and changing files and folders. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.game-folder.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: The linked game installation folder. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.game-textures.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: The Game textures look of the preview, made from the linked game’s own graphics. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.source.app.meaning: The quiet source word at the start of an Output row: says where the message comes from. Here: The app itself. Keep it to one or two short words.

output.constructs.heading.meaning: Headline of the list, inside a run group, of the script commands this run used in a way no recorded game map has used, so the map may differ from the game there.

output.constructs.more.meaning: Last item of the list of commands not compared against the game, when more were counted than named.

placeholders.count: a count, shown as digits

Includes are files a map loads with #include or #include_drs; the script is the map being run. explorer.create.definition-file.meaning: Explorer folder menu item that opens the Definition File dialog for this folder; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.

explorer.create.script.meaning: Item of the Explorer folder menu and of the folder's create (+) menu that creates a new random map script (.rms) in the folder.

explorer.create.map-test-script.meaning: Item of the Explorer folder menu and of the folder's create (+) menu that creates a new map-test script (.rmstest), which generates a map many times and checks it.

explorer.create.xs-script.meaning: Item of the Explorer folder menu and of the folder's create (+) menu that creates a new XS script (.xs). XS stays as written.

explorer.create.folder.meaning: Item of the Explorer folder menu and of the folder's create (+) menu that creates a new folder inside it.

explorer.create.label.meaning: Accessible name of the + button on an Explorer folder row that opens the menu to create a script or folder in it.

placeholders.name: the folder's name, such as Maps

explorer.label.meaning: Accessible name of the File Explorer side panel, which lists the open folder's files.

explorer.search.label.meaning: Accessible name of the search box at the top of the Explorer that finds files in the open folder by name.

explorer.search.placeholder.meaning: Grey hint text inside the empty Explorer search box.

explorer.search.clear.meaning: Accessible name of the small x button that empties the Explorer search box.

explorer.search.searching.meaning: Accessible name of the placeholder rows shown while an Explorer search runs and has no results yet.

explorer.search.no-results.rms.meaning: Shown in the Explorer when no file of the open folder matches the search. RMS (random map script) stays as written.

explorer.search.no-results.meaning: Shown in the Explorer when no file of the open folder matches the search, in the edition that edits XS scripts only.

explorer.open-file.label.meaning: Accessible name of the Explorer toolbar icon button that opens files with the Windows file picker.

explorer.open-file.tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the Explorer toolbar icon button that opens files; same words as File → Open File in the menu, without the ellipsis.

explorer.open-folder.label.meaning: Accessible name of the Explorer toolbar icon button that opens a folder in the Explorer.

explorer.open-folder.tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the Explorer toolbar icon button that opens a folder; same words as File → Open Folder in the menu, without the ellipsis.

explorer.tree.label.meaning: Accessible name of the Explorer's file tree for the open folder.

placeholders.name: the open folder's name, such as Maps

explorer.empty.maps.message: Open a folder to browse and edit its maps.
explorer.empty.maps.meaning: One muted line in the Explorer while no folder is open; the toolbar's Open Folder button opens one.

explorer.empty.scripts.message: Open a folder to browse and edit its scripts.
explorer.empty.scripts.meaning: One muted line in the Explorer while no folder is open, in the edition that edits XS scripts only; the toolbar's Open Folder button opens one.

explorer.indexing.meaning: Accessible name of the placeholder rows shown while the Explorer reads a folder's entries.

explorer.read-failed.message: This folder could not be read
explorer.read-failed.meaning: Shown in the Explorer tree in place of a folder's entries when they could not be read, when no more specific message applies.

explorer.context.open-in-explorer.meaning: Explorer folder menu item that shows the folder in Windows File Explorer (the Windows program, not this panel).

explorer.context.rename.meaning: Explorer menu item that lets the user type a new name for the file or folder.

explorer.context.delete.meaning: Explorer menu item that deletes the file or folder after a confirmation (to the Recycle Bin unless Skip Recycle Bin When Deleting is on).

explorer.inline.create-file.meaning: Accessible name of the name field shown in the Explorer tree while creating a new file.

explorer.inline.create-folder.meaning: Accessible name of the name field shown in the Explorer tree while creating a new folder.

explorer.inline.rename-file.meaning: Accessible name of the name field shown in the Explorer tree while renaming a file.

explorer.inline.rename-folder.meaning: Accessible name of the name field shown in the Explorer tree while renaming a folder.

definition-file.title.meaning: Title of the dialog that writes an .inc file of the selected game version’s object and terrain names.

definition-file.close-label.meaning: Accessible name of the dialog’s close button.

definition-file.loading.message: Reading the names of the selected game version…
definition-file.loading.meaning: Shown while the dialog gathers the names it can write.

definition-file.identity.game-version.meaning: Label of the game version the file is generated for.

definition-file.identity.game-version.un.meaning: A game version whose results have not been compared against the game.

placeholders.version: the game version, such as 101.103.60000.0 (not translated)

definition-file.identity.target.meaning: Label of the folder the file will be written into: the open folder (shown with a trailing slash), or a Save dialog that follows. Shown only when the dialog was opened from the File menu.

definition-file.target.save-dialog.meaning: Without an open folder, a Save dialog asks where to write the file after Generate.

definition-file.groups.label.meaning: Accessible name of the list of content groups the file can hold.

definition-file.group.terrains.meaning: Content group of terrain names and their IDs.

definition-file.group.terrains.descripti.message: Terrain IDs for terrain_type, base_terrain, and other terrain settings
definition-file.group.terrains.descripti.meaning: Describes the terrain group. terrain_type and base_terrain are RMS attributes and stay as written.

definition-file.group.objects.meaning: Content group of object names and their IDs.

definition-file.group.objects.descriptio.message: Object IDs for create_object and other object settings
definition-file.group.objects.descriptio.meaning: Describes the object group. create_object is an RMS command and stays as written.

definition-file.group.count.meaning: How many names the group writes with the current choices.

placeholders.count: the number of names

definition-file.built-in.meaning: Also writes the names the game already defines.

definition-file.built-in.description.message: Names the game already defines. Scripts can use them without this file.

definition-file.note.no-game-folder.message: Link your game folder to add names for the objects and terrains the game leaves unnamed.
definition-file.note.no-game-folder.meaning: Without a linked game folder only the game’s built-in names are available.

definition-file.note.other-version.message: Your game folder has another game version, so its names aren’t used.
definition-file.note.other-version.meaning: Names from the game folder are used only for the game version it has.

definition-file.note.no-text.message: The names in your game folder can’t be read for this game version.
definition-file.note.no-text.meaning: The game folder’s display names are unreadable, so only built-in names are available.

definition-file.note.nothing-new.message: Every named object and terrain already has a built-in name.
definition-file.note.nothing-new.meaning: The game folder adds no name the game lacks; the built-in names option can still write them.

definition-file.note.left-out.project.message: {count, plural, one {# built-in name is left out because a script in this folder already defines it.} other {# built-in names are left out because scripts in this folder already define them.}}
definition-file.note.left-out.project.meaning: Built-in names the open folder’s scripts define themselves are not written again.

placeholders.count: the number of names left out

definition-file.note.left-out.unique.message: {count, plural, one {# name from the game folder is left out because no unique name was left for it.} other {# names from the game folder are left out because no unique name was left for them.}}
definition-file.note.left-out.unique.meaning: Names that would collide with another name even after adding the ID are not written.

placeholders.count: the number of names left out

definition-file.note.project-partial.message: Some scripts in this folder couldn’t be checked for names they already define.
definition-file.note.project-partial.meaning: The check of the folder’s own definitions stopped at its size limits.

definition-file.notes.more.meaning: Quiet count after the one note shown left of the Generate button, when the dialog has more notes; hovering or focusing the note lists them all.

placeholders.count: how many more notes the tooltip lists

definition-file.unavailable.incomplete.message: No Definition File can be generated for the selected game version, because its game data is incomplete.
definition-file.unavailable.incomplete.meaning: The selected content is a test fixture or otherwise incomplete, so no list of its names is offered.

definition-file.unavailable.no-content.message: No game version is available to generate a Definition File for.
definition-file.unavailable.no-content.meaning: No game data could be selected.

definition-file.unavailable.failed.message: The names of the selected game version couldn’t be read.
definition-file.unavailable.failed.meaning: Gathering the names failed; Output has the details.

definition-file.file-name.label.meaning: Label of the editable name of the file to write.

definition-file.file-name.empty.meaning: The file name field is empty.

definition-file.file-name.invalid.message: This name can’t be used for a file in Windows.
definition-file.file-name.invalid.meaning: The file name has characters or a form Windows does not allow.

definition-file.file-name.extension.message: The file name must end in .inc.
definition-file.file-name.extension.meaning: A Definition File is an RMS include file; .inc stays as written.

definition-file.file-name.reserved.message: This name belongs to a game library file. Choose another name.
definition-file.file-name.reserved.meaning: The name is one of the game’s own include files, which the game would load instead.

definition-file.generate.meaning: Writes the file into the folder shown.

definition-file.generate.save-dialog.meaning: Asks where to save, then writes the file; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.

definition-file.error.message: The Definition File couldn’t be written. Output has the details.

definition-file.replace.title.meaning: Asks before overwriting an existing file of the same name.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as definitions.inc

definition-file.replace.description.message: A file with this name is already in {folder}. Replacing it overwrites its contents.
definition-file.replace.description.meaning: Explains what replacing the file does.

definition-file.output.failed.message: The Definition File could not be written
definition-file.output.failed.meaning: Output headline when writing a Definition File failed.

definition-file.output.unavailable.message: The names for a Definition File could not be read
definition-file.output.unavailable.meaning: Output headline when the Definition File dialog could not gather its names.

definition-file.save-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the Windows Save dialog for a Definition File.

definition-file.save-dialog.filter.meaning: File type name in the Windows Save dialog.

deploy-panel.enable-mod.meaning: Option beside the Deploy mod button, on by default and remembered: after deploying, the IDE turns the mod on in the game's own list of mods.

deploy-panel.enable-mod.tooltip.message: Turns the mod on in the game's mod list. The map and its icon appear after the game restarts.
deploy-panel.enable-mod.tooltip.meaning: Explains the Enable mod option. The game shows a new local mod's maps and map icons only once the mod is enabled and the game has restarted.

deploy-panel.success.enabled.message: The mod is enabled. Restart the game to see the map and its icon.
deploy-panel.success.enabled.meaning: Line in the deployment's success confirmation when the mod is enabled in the game's mod list. The game shows new maps and icons only after a restart.

deploy-panel.success.enable-yourself.message: Enable the mod in the game under Mods → My Mods, then restart the game to see the map and its icon.
deploy-panel.success.enable-yourself.meaning: Line in the deployment's success confirmation when the IDE did not enable the mod (Enable mod was off, or enabling failed). “Mods → My Mods” names the game's own menu and its tab; use the game's wording in the translation.

deploy-panel.success.enable-failed.message: {reason, select, malformed {The mod was not enabled: the game's mod list file could not be read.} unexpected-layout {The mod was not enabled: the game's mod list file has a layout the IDE does not know.} duplicate-entry {The mod was not enabled: the game's mod list names this mod more than once.} unexpected-entry {The mod was not enabled: the game's entry for this mod has a layout the IDE does not know.} changed {The mod was not enabled: the game changed its mod list at the same time.} unsafe-path {The mod was not enabled: the profile's mods folder or mod list is a link to another place.} other {The mod was not enabled: the game's mod list could not be saved.}}
deploy-panel.success.enable-failed.meaning: Line in the deployment's success confirmation when the mod was deployed but could not be enabled in the game's mod list; the reason picks the sentence. The mod list file was left as it was.

placeholders.reason: why the mod list was left unchanged (a fixed keyword, never shown)

deploy-panel.success.game-running.message: The game is running: the change applies after a restart, and the game may undo it when it closes. If the mod is off after the restart, close the game and deploy again.
deploy-panel.success.game-running.meaning: Warning in the deployment's success confirmation when the IDE enabled the mod while the linked game was running. The game may write its own mod list when it closes.

deploy-panel.success.open-folder.meaning: Button in the deployment's success confirmation: opens the game's local mods folder in Windows Explorer with the deployed mod's folder selected.

deploy-panel.success.finish.meaning: Primary button that closes the deployment's success confirmation (Enter).

deploy-panel.success.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation shown after the mod was deployed.

deploy-panel.success.saved-to.meaning: Line above the read-only field showing the deployed mod's folder path; the path follows on its own line.

deploy-panel.success.path.meaning: Accessible name of the read-only field showing the deployed mod's folder path.

deploy-panel.success.path.copy.meaning: Accessible name of the deployed mod path field's copy button.

deploy-panel.success.path.copied.meaning: Accessible name of the deployed mod path field's copy button for a moment after it copied the path.

deploy-panel.output.cause.enabled.message: {count, plural, one {# file.} other {# files.}} The mod is enabled; restart the game to see the map and its icon.
deploy-panel.output.cause.enabled.meaning: Cause line of the Output note for a finished deployment when the mod is enabled in the game's mod list.

placeholders.count: the number of files the mod holds

deploy-panel.output.cause.enable-yoursel.message: {count, plural, one {# file.} other {# files.}} Enable the mod in the game under Mods → My Mods, then restart the game to see the map and its icon.
deploy-panel.output.cause.enable-yoursel.meaning: Cause line of the Output note for a finished deployment when the IDE did not enable the mod. “Mods → My Mods” names the game's own menu and its tab; use the game's wording in the translation.

placeholders.count: the number of files the mod holds

deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.message: The mod was deployed but not enabled
deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.meaning: Output warning headline: the mod's files were deployed, but the game's mod list could not be changed to enable it.

deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.cause.message: {reason, select, malformed {The game's mod list file could not be read, so it was left unchanged.} unexpected-layout {The game's mod list file has a layout the IDE does not know, so it was left unchanged.} duplicate-entry {The game's mod list names this mod more than once, so it was left unchanged.} unexpected-entry {The game's entry for this mod has a layout the IDE does not know, so it was left unchanged.} changed {The game changed its mod list at the same time, so the list was left as the game wrote it.} unsafe-path {The profile's mods folder or mod list is a link to another place, so it was left unchanged.} other {The game's mod list could not be saved; the previous list is still in place.}}
deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.cause.meaning: Why the game's mod list was left unchanged; the reason picks the sentence.

placeholders.reason: why the mod list was left unchanged (a fixed keyword, never shown)

deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.action.message: Enable the mod in the game under Mods → My Mods, then restart the game
deploy-panel.output.enable-failed.action.meaning: Next step after the IDE could not enable a deployed mod. “Mods → My Mods” names the game's own menu and its tab; use the game's wording in the translation.

deploy-panel.output.game-running.message: The mod list changed while the game is running
deploy-panel.output.game-running.meaning: Output warning headline: the IDE enabled the mod in the game's mod list while the linked game was running.

deploy-panel.output.game-running.cause.message: The change applies after a restart, and the game may undo it when it closes. If the mod is off after the restart, close the game and deploy again.
deploy-panel.output.game-running.cause.meaning: Why the change may not last: the game may write its own mod list when it closes.

deploy-panel.output.preview-reused.meaning: Output note when the Deploy as mod dialog uses the map the preview already shows instead of generating it again.

placeholders.name: the script file name, such as Arabia.rms

deploy-panel.output.preview-regenerating.message: The current preview could not be reused, so it is generated again
deploy-panel.output.preview-regenerating.meaning: Output note when the Deploy as mod dialog could not use the map the preview shows and generates the map again.

deploy-panel.output.source-failed.message: This map could not be generated for deployment
deploy-panel.output.source-failed.meaning: Output headline when the map of the script being deployed failed to generate for a reason without its own message.

deploy-panel.output.deployed.meaning: Output note after a mod was deployed.

placeholders.mod: the mod's folder name, such as MyRMSMod
placeholders.profile: the profile's folder name, a long number such as 76561198000000001

deploy-panel.open-folder.failed.message: The mods folder could not be opened
deploy-panel.open-folder.failed.meaning: Output headline when Open mods folder in the deployment's success confirmation failed.

deploy-panel.target.open-folder.message: Open target directory in Windows Explorer
deploy-panel.target.open-folder.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the icon-only button right of the Target directory field: opens the game profile's local mods folder in Windows Explorer (before the first deployment creates it, the nearest existing folder above it). “Target directory” is the field's label; “Windows Explorer” is the Windows program, use its usual name in the translation.

deploy-panel.target.open-folder.failed.message: The target directory could not be opened
deploy-panel.target.open-folder.failed.meaning: Output headline when the deployment panel's Open target directory button failed to open the folder in Windows Explorer.

deploy-panel.target.meaning: Label and accessible name of the read-only field showing the folder the mod is placed in (the profile's local mods folder).

deploy-panel.target.copy.meaning: Accessible name of the Target directory field's copy button.

deploy-panel.target.copied.meaning: Accessible name of the Target directory field's copy button for a moment after it copied the folder path.

deploy-panel.title.meaning: Title of the dialog that deploys the open random map script into the game as a local mod.

deploy-panel.close.meaning: Accessible name of the Deploy as mod dialog's icon-only close button.

deploy-panel.select-game-folder.meaning: Shown with the Select game folder button when no game folder is linked: deploying needs the game's profile folders.

deploy-panel.source.meaning: Label and accessible name of the select that chooses which open random map script (.rms or .rms2 main file) is deployed. RMS is the script format's name and stays as written.

deploy-panel.source.placeholder.meaning: Shown in the RMS source select when no random map script is open. RMS stays as written.

deploy-panel.source.failed.message: This map could not be generated, so it cannot be deployed yet. Fix the problem shown in Output, then open Deploy as Mod again.
deploy-panel.source.failed.meaning: Error line when the chosen script's map failed to generate. Output is the panel that lists messages; Deploy as Mod is the menu command that opens this dialog: use the names the interface uses for them.

deploy-panel.source.failed.guidance.message: This map could not be generated, so it cannot be deployed yet. {guidance}
deploy-panel.source.failed.guidance.meaning: Error line when the chosen script's map failed to generate for a known reason; the reason and what to do follow.

placeholders.guidance: one or more sentences saying what went wrong and what to do, such as "P3 has no player land. ..."

deploy-panel.source.cancelled.message: The preview of the selected RMS source was cancelled.
deploy-panel.source.cancelled.meaning: Error line when the map generation the dialog started for the chosen script was stopped. RMS source is the select's label.

deploy-panel.mod-name.meaning: Label and accessible name of the field for the mod's folder name.

deploy-panel.mod-name.history.meaning: Accessible name of the icon-only button beside the Mod name field that lists the names of mods this script was deployed as before.

deploy-panel.profile.meaning: Label and accessible name of the select that chooses the game's user profile (a numbered profile folder) the mod is deployed into.

deploy-panel.profile.placeholder.meaning: Shown in the User profile select before a profile is chosen, and in the Target directory field, which shows a folder only once a profile is chosen.

deploy-panel.profile.suggested.meaning: An option of the User profile select: the profile the IDE suggests (the one the game used last). Keep the separator style of the language.

placeholders.profile: the profile's folder name, a long number such as 76561198000000001 (not translated)

deploy-panel.tree.meaning: Accessible name of the tree listing every file the mod will hold.

deploy-panel.tree.loading.meaning: Accessible name of the placeholder shown while the list of the mod's files is computed.

deploy-panel.no-source.message: Open an .rms or .rms2 main file to deploy.
deploy-panel.no-source.meaning: Shown in place of the file tree when no random map script is open. .rms and .rms2 are file extensions and stay as written.

deploy-panel.constructs.label.meaning: Accessible name of the quiet note beside Deploy mod that says how many script commands were not compared against the game, followed by their names.

placeholders.note: the note, such as "3 commands not compared against the game"
placeholders.names: the list of command names (RMS commands, not translated)

deploy-panel.deploy.meaning: Primary button that deploys the mod into the chosen profile.

deploy-panel.replace.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation shown when a mod of the same name already exists in the profile.

deploy-panel.replace.description.message: Every file from the existing mod {name} will be removed.
deploy-panel.replace.description.meaning: Explains what replacing the existing mod does. The name is shown in bold.

placeholders.name: the mod's folder name, such as MyRMSMod

deploy-panel.replace.confirm.meaning: Confirms replacing the existing mod: its files are removed and the new ones deployed.

problems-panel.log.label.meaning: Accessible name of the Problems list: how many problem rows it shows. (English keeps the plural word for one problem too.)

placeholders.count: how many problem rows the list shows

problems-panel.empty.meaning: Shown in the empty Problems tab when the open scripts have no diagnostics.

problems-panel.empty.filtered.message: No problems match the filter ({hidden} hidden).
problems-panel.empty.filtered.meaning: Shown in the Problems tab when the severity filter hides every problem.

placeholders.hidden: how many problems the filter hides

problems-panel.severity.error.meaning: The severity word at the start of a Problems row.

problems-panel.severity.warning.meaning: The severity word at the start of a Problems row.

problems-panel.severity.info.meaning: The severity word at the start of a Problems row (an informational note).

problems-panel.group.file.meaning: The quiet word at the start of a file group header in Problems: the problems below are in this script file.

problems-panel.group.game-file.meaning: The quiet word at the start of a file group header in Problems for a file of the game itself, which the user cannot edit.

problems-panel.group.errors.meaning: Count in a Problems file group header, between middle dots (“arabia.rms · 2 errors · 1 warning”).

placeholders.count: a count, shown as digits

problems-panel.group.warnings.meaning: Count in a Problems file group header, between middle dots.

placeholders.count: a count, shown as digits

problems-panel.group.notes.meaning: Count in a Problems file group header, between middle dots (informational notes).

placeholders.count: a count, shown as digits

problems-panel.group.show.meaning: Accessible name of the chevron that opens a file group in Problems.

placeholders.file: the script file name, such as arabia.rms

problems-panel.group.hide.meaning: Accessible name of the chevron that closes a file group in Problems.

placeholders.file: the script file name, such as arabia.rms

problems-panel.group.label.meaning: Accessible name of the rows of one file group in Problems.

severity-filter.label.meaning: Accessible name of the group of three severity toggles in the Output or Problems header.

severity-filter.errors.label.meaning: Accessible name of the icon toggle that shows or hides error rows; its pressed state says whether they show.

severity-filter.errors.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the error toggle while errors are shown.

severity-filter.warnings.label.meaning: Accessible name of the icon toggle that shows or hides warning rows; its pressed state says whether they show.

severity-filter.warnings.show.meaning: Tooltip of the warning toggle while warnings are hidden.

severity-filter.warnings.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the warning toggle while warnings are shown.

severity-filter.notes.label.meaning: Accessible name of the icon toggle that shows or hides informational note rows; its pressed state says whether they show.

severity-filter.notes.show.meaning: Tooltip of the note toggle while notes are hidden.

severity-filter.notes.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the note toggle while notes are shown.

linked-game.installed-maps.root-unreadab.message: The maps in {folder} could not be listed: {error}
linked-game.installed-maps.root-unreadab.meaning: Output note of the Installed Maps browser when one folder of maps in the linked game or a mod could not be read. The error is the system’s own English words.

placeholders.folder: the folder, as a path inside the game or profile (such as mods/local/MyMod/resources/_common/random-map-scripts)
placeholders.error: the reason in English, as the system gave it

linked-game.installed-maps.installation-.message: An installation with missing or unreadable game files was skipped.
linked-game.installed-maps.installation-.meaning: Output warning when listing installed random maps: one game installation was left out because its game files are missing or unreadable.
Output warning when listing installed random maps: one game installation was left out because its folder cannot be reached.

linked-game.installed-maps.root-limit.message: Installed-source root count reached its safety limit.
linked-game.installed-maps.root-limit.meaning: Output warning when listing installed random maps: there are more map folders (installation and mod folders) than the IDE lists, so the rest are left out.

linked-game.installed-maps.entry-limit.message: Installed-source entry count reached its safety limit.
linked-game.installed-maps.entry-limit.meaning: Output warning when listing installed random maps: there are more map files than the IDE lists, so the rest are left out.

linked-game.unverified-version.meaning: Names a game version the IDE has not verified, inside a sentence about the game data of the linked game folder. AoE2DE is the game's short name and stays as written.

placeholders.version: the game's version number, such as 101.103.54800.0

linked-game.content-read.meaning: Output headline: previews use the objects and terrains read from the linked game folder for this game version.

placeholders.label: the game version, such as AoE2DE 101.103.54800.0 (not verified)

linked-game.content-read.cause.loaded.meaning: Cause line after the game data was used: how many objects it names; it was read before, so nothing was read again.

placeholders.objects: how many objects the game data names

linked-game.content-read.cause.read.message: {objects, plural, other {{objects} objects, read in {milliseconds} ms.}}
linked-game.content-read.cause.read.meaning: Cause line after the game data was read: how many objects it names and how long reading took, in milliseconds (ms).

placeholders.objects: how many objects the game data names
placeholders.milliseconds: how long reading took, in milliseconds

linked-game.content-unreadable.message: The game data of {label} could not be read
linked-game.content-unreadable.meaning: Output warning headline: the objects and terrains of the linked game folder could not be read for this game version.

placeholders.label: the game version, such as AoE2DE 101.103.54800.0 (not verified)

linked-game.content-unreadable.cause.message: Previews of that version use the packaged {version} data, where objects and terrains added later cannot generate.
linked-game.content-unreadable.cause.meaning: Cause line when the game data could not be read: previews fall back to the game data packaged with the IDE, which lacks objects and terrains the game added later.

placeholders.version: the version number of the packaged game data, such as 101.103.48987.0

lint-rule.RMS4003.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4003 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4003)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

lint-rule.RMS4005.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4005 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4005)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

lint-rule.RMS4006.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4006 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4006)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

lint-rule.RMS4008.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4008 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4008)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

lint-rule.RMS4009.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4009 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4009)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

lint-rule.RMS4010.title.message: Number where a name is needed
lint-rule.RMS4010.title.meaning: Name of the RMS lint rule RMS4010 in View → Lint Rules (shown as “name (RMS4010)”; its check mark turns the rule on or off for the open workspace).

The rule marks a name (a #define or #const) that some random or conditional paths of the script leave undefined where a command reads it.

map-icon.generate.meaning: Toggle above the map icon frame: on, the IDE draws the map's icon (the picture the game shows for the map) and deploys it; off, an icon file next to the script is kept.

map-icon.open-larger.meaning: Accessible name of the map icon frame, a button that opens the larger map icon view.

map-icon.save-image.meaning: Accessible name of the icon-only button that saves the map icon as a PNG file.

map-icon.save-image.tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the icon-only button that saves the map icon as a PNG file; the ellipsis says a Save dialog follows.

map-icon.frame.generating.meaning: Accessible name of the map icon picture while its map is being generated.

map-icon.frame.ready.meaning: Accessible name of the map icon picture when it shows the generated icon.

map-icon.frame.original.meaning: Accessible name of the map icon picture when it shows the icon file found next to the script.

map-icon.frame.original-unavailable.message: Original map icon cannot be displayed
map-icon.frame.original-unavailable.meaning: Accessible name of the empty map icon picture when the icon file next to the script cannot be shown (it is still deployed).

map-icon.frame.none.meaning: Accessible name of the empty map icon picture when there is no icon to show.

map-icon.switch.no-source.message: Open an .rms or .rms2 main file to generate a map icon.
map-icon.switch.no-source.meaning: Why Generate map icon cannot be switched: no script is open. .rms and .rms2 are file extensions and stay as written.

map-icon.switch.needs-preview.message: Map icon generation needs a successful preview of this source.
map-icon.switch.needs-preview.meaning: Why Generate map icon cannot be switched on: the script's map has not generated successfully.

map-icon.switch.unavailable.meaning: Why Generate map icon cannot be switched on: drawing the icon failed.

placeholders.reason: why drawing the icon failed, in one or more sentences

map-icon.status.unavailable.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame when drawing the icon failed.

placeholders.reason: why drawing the icon failed, in one or more sentences

map-icon.status.generating-seed.message: Map icon: generating the map from seed {seed}
map-icon.status.generating-seed.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame while the icon's own map generates with a seed the user chose.

placeholders.seed: the seed, a whole number up to 4294967295 (shown as written)

map-icon.status.needs-preview.message: Map icon needs a successful preview of this source.
map-icon.status.needs-preview.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame when the script's map has not generated successfully.

map-icon.status.rendering.message: Map icon: rendering from the current preview
map-icon.status.rendering.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame while the icon is drawn from the generated map.

map-icon.status.waiting.message: Map icon: waiting for the deployment preview
map-icon.status.waiting.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame while the list of the mod's files is computed.

map-icon.status.generated-replacing.message: Map icon: generated {file}, replacing the original in this deployed snapshot only
map-icon.status.generated-replacing.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame: the deployed mod gets the generated icon instead of the icon file next to the script, which stays unchanged.

placeholders.file: the icon file name, such as Arabia.png

map-icon.status.generated.message: Map icon: generated {file} from the current preview
map-icon.status.generated.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame: the deployed mod gets the icon drawn from the generated map.

placeholders.file: the icon file name, such as Arabia.png

map-icon.status.original.message: Map icon: original {file} from the source folder
map-icon.status.original.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame: the deployed mod gets the icon file found next to the script.

placeholders.file: the icon file name, such as Arabia.png

map-icon.status.none.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame: the deployed mod has no map icon.

map-icon.status.with-fallback.meaning: Tooltip and accessible description of the map icon frame when the chosen Game textures look is unavailable: the icon's status, then the note saying so.

placeholders.status: the icon's status sentence, such as "Map icon: none"
placeholders.note: the sentence saying the icon uses texture colors instead

map-icon.tree.generated.meaning: Shown in parentheses after the icon file in the list of the mod's files: the IDE drew this icon.

map-icon.tree.original.meaning: Shown in parentheses after the icon file in the list of the mod's files: the icon file found next to the script.

map-icon.render-failed.message: The map icon could not be drawn
map-icon.render-failed.meaning: First sentence of the reason when drawing the map icon failed; shown in the map icon's tooltip.

map-icon.output.options-not-remembered.message: Map icon options were not remembered
map-icon.output.options-not-remembered.meaning: Output warning when the map icon's view and drawing choices could not be stored for the next time.

map-icon.output.seed-failed.message: The map icon from seed {seed} could not be generated
map-icon.output.seed-failed.meaning: Output headline when generating the map icon's own map with a chosen seed failed; the previous icon stays.

placeholders.seed: the seed, a whole number up to 4294967295 (shown as written)

map-icon.output.saved.meaning: Output note after Save image saved the map icon.

placeholders.name: the saved file name, such as Arabia.png

map-icon.output.save-failed.message: The map icon could not be saved
map-icon.output.save-failed.meaning: Output headline when Save image failed.

map-icon.lightbox.close.meaning: Accessible name of the larger map icon view's icon-only close button.

map-icon.lightbox.title.meaning: Title of the larger map icon view when the icon has no file name yet (otherwise the file name is the title).

map-icon.view-tools.meaning: Accessible name of the group of buttons over the larger icon that change its perspective, look, and terrain relief.

map-icon.perspective.diamond.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the perspective button while the icon shows the map turned 45 degrees, as the game's minimap does.

map-icon.perspective.top-down.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the perspective button while the icon shows the map straight from above, as a square.

map-icon.look.minimap.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the look button while the icon uses the colors of the game's minimap.

map-icon.look.texture-colors.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the look button while the icon uses one average color per terrain texture.

map-icon.look.game-textures.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the look button while the icon is drawn with the terrain textures of the user's own linked game.

map-icon.look.pending.meaning: Tooltip of the look button while the textures of the user's linked game are prepared for the icon.

map-icon.look.fallback.message: Game textures are unavailable, so the icon uses texture colors.
map-icon.look.fallback.meaning: Note added to the map icon's tooltip when the chosen Game textures look cannot be used. Game textures and texture colors name two looks of the look button.

map-icon.relief.meaning: Accessible name of the toggle that shades the icon by terrain height; its pressed state says whether the shading shows.

map-icon.relief.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the terrain relief toggle while the shading shows: what clicking does.

map-icon.relief.show.meaning: Tooltip of the terrain relief toggle while the shading is off: what clicking does.

map-icon.terrain-smoothing.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the toggle that blends neighboring terrains in the icon instead of drawing hard tile edges.

map-icon.random-seed.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the icon-only button that generates the icon's map again with a random seed.

map-icon.use-editor-seed.meaning: Button that returns the icon to the map generated with the seed set in the editor's run settings.

map-icon.seed.meaning: Accessible name of the field with the seed the icon's map is generated with.

map-icon.seed.placeholder.meaning: Shown in the empty seed field: the editor's own seed is used.

map-icon.spawn-markers.player-squares.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the spawn marker button while each player's start shows as a square in the player's color.

map-icon.spawn-markers.nomad-feet.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the spawn marker button while each player's start shows as footprints, as on Nomad maps.

map-icon.spawn-markers.hidden.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the spawn marker button while players' starts are not marked.

map-icon.spawn-size.meaning: Accessible name of the number between the minus and plus buttons that sets the spawn markers' size.

map-icon.spawn-size.decrease.meaning: Accessible name of the minus button beside the spawn marker size.

map-icon.spawn-size.increase.meaning: Accessible name of the plus button beside the spawn marker size.

map-icon.spawn-size.value.meaning: The spawn marker size shown between the minus and plus buttons, as a percentage of the map width. Use the language's usual percent form.

map-icon.spawn-size.value-text.meaning: What assistive technology reads as the spawn marker size's value.

map-icon.spawn-size.tooltip.message: Spawn marker size (% of the map width)
map-icon.spawn-size.tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the spawn marker size: the number is a percentage of the map width.

map-icon.art.trees.show.meaning: Accessible name of the toggle that draws trees on the icon, and its tooltip while trees are hidden (what clicking does).

map-icon.art.trees.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the trees toggle while trees are drawn: what clicking does.

map-icon.art.trees.options.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the arrow beside the trees toggle that opens the trees' amount and size sliders.

map-icon.art.trees.amount.meaning: Accessible name of the slider for how many trees the icon draws. Lower case, as English reads it after the slider's role.

map-icon.art.trees.size.meaning: Accessible name of the slider for how large the icon draws trees. Lower case, as English reads it after the slider's role.

map-icon.art.resources.show.meaning: Accessible name of the toggle that draws gold and stone mines on the icon, and its tooltip while they are hidden (what clicking does).

map-icon.art.resources.hide.meaning: Tooltip of the gold and stone toggle while they are drawn: what clicking does.

map-icon.art.resources.options.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the arrow beside the gold and stone toggle that opens their amount and size sliders.

map-icon.art.resources.amount.meaning: Accessible name of the slider for how many gold and stone mines the icon draws. Lower case, as English reads it after the slider's role.

map-icon.art.resources.size.meaning: Accessible name of the slider for how large the icon draws gold and stone mines. Lower case, as English reads it after the slider's role.

map-icon.art.amount.fewer.meaning: Word at the left end of an amount slider (fewer sprites).

map-icon.art.amount.more.meaning: Word at the right end of an amount slider (more sprites).

map-icon.art.amount.one-per-kind.meaning: Spoken value of an amount slider at its left end: one sprite for each kind of object.

map-icon.art.amount.one-per-object.meaning: Spoken value of an amount slider at its right end: a sprite for every object.

map-icon.art.amount.few.meaning: Spoken value of an amount slider in its lower third.

map-icon.art.amount.medium.meaning: Spoken value of an amount slider in its middle third (a medium amount).

map-icon.art.amount.many.meaning: Spoken value of an amount slider in its upper third.

map-icon.art.size.smaller.meaning: Word at the left end of a size slider (smaller sprites).

map-icon.art.size.larger.meaning: Word at the right end of a size slider (larger sprites).

map-icon.art.size.smallest.meaning: Spoken value of a size slider at its left end.

map-icon.art.size.small.meaning: Spoken value of a size slider below its middle.

map-icon.art.size.medium.meaning: Spoken value of a size slider at its middle (a medium size).

map-icon.art.size.large.meaning: Spoken value of a size slider above its middle.

map-icon.art.size.largest.meaning: Spoken value of a size slider at its right end.

map-icon.art.spawn-overlap.meaning: Check item under the sliders: also draw the sprites that a spawn marker covers.

workbench.application-menu.label.meaning: Accessible name of the menu bar (File, Edit, View, Help) in the window title bar.

workbench.explorer.collapse.meaning: Accessible name of the title-bar button that hides the file explorer side panel.

workbench.explorer.expand.meaning: Accessible name of the title-bar button that shows the file explorer side panel again.

workbench.explorer.collapse-tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the title-bar button that hides the Explorer (the file explorer side panel). "Explorer" is the panel's name.

workbench.explorer.expand-tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the title-bar button that shows the Explorer (the file explorer side panel) again. "Explorer" is the panel's name.

workbench.explorer.resize.meaning: Accessible name of the splitter between the file explorer and the editor; dragging it or pressing the arrow keys changes the explorer's width.

workbench.preview.resize.meaning: Accessible name of the splitter between the code editor and the live map preview; dragging it or pressing the arrow keys changes the preview's width.

workbench.preview.stages-shown-next-run.message: Live generation stages shown from the next run
workbench.preview.stages-shown-next-run.meaning: Output note after View > Show Live Generation Stages was turned on while a map was generating: the running generation keeps its setting, the next run shows the map's stages as they are generated.

workbench.preview.stages-hidden-next-run.message: Live generation stages hidden from the next run
workbench.preview.stages-hidden-next-run.meaning: Output note after View > Show Live Generation Stages was turned off while a map was generating: the running generation keeps its setting, the next run shows only the finished map.

workbench.bottom-panel.label.meaning: Accessible name of the bottom panel's header row that holds the Output and Problems tabs.

workbench.bottom-panel.label-with-test-r.message: Problems, output, and test results panel
workbench.bottom-panel.label-with-test-r.meaning: Accessible name of the bottom panel's header row when it also offers the Test Results tab (map tests).

workbench.bottom-panel.resize.meaning: Accessible name of the splitter at the top of the bottom panel; dragging it or pressing the arrow keys changes the panel's height.

workbench.bottom-panel.tab.output.meaning: Tab of the Output panel (messages of runs, saves, and other actions), led by the number of messages it holds as a count badge. "Output" is the panel's name; keep it a short label, not a sentence.

placeholders.count: the number of messages in the Output panel, such as 12

workbench.bottom-panel.tab.problems.meaning: Tab of the Problems panel (errors and warnings found in the open scripts), led by the number of problems as a count badge. "Problems" is the panel's name; keep it a short label, not a sentence.

placeholders.count: the number of problems found in the open scripts, such as 3

workbench.bottom-panel.tab.test-results.meaning: Tab of the Test Results panel of a map test (a script that generates many maps and checks them), led by the number of findings as a count badge. "Test Results" is the panel's name; keep it a short label, not a sentence.

placeholders.count: the number of findings of the map test, such as 2

workbench.bottom-panel.output.meaning: The Output panel's name, inserted into the accessible name of its severity filter (the toggles that show or hide errors, warnings, and notes).

workbench.bottom-panel.problems.meaning: The Problems panel's name, inserted into the accessible name of its severity filter (the toggles that show or hide errors, warnings, and notes).

workbench.native.restart-label.meaning: Accessible name of the button in the bottom panel's header that restarts a background process of the app after it stopped unexpectedly. Keep {name} as written.

placeholders.name: the name of a background process of the app, such as rms-ls or rmsd (a program name; shown as written)

workbench.native.failed.meaning: Tooltip of the restart button of a stopped background process when the process gave no reason. Keep {name} as written.

placeholders.name: the name of a background process of the app, such as rms-ls or rmsd (a program name; shown as written)

workbench.native.restarted.meaning: Output note after the user restarted a background process of the app that had stopped. Keep {name} as written.

placeholders.name: the name of a background process of the app, such as rms-ls or rmsd (a program name; shown as written)

workbench.native.restart-failed.meaning: Output headline when restarting a stopped background process of the app failed. Keep {name} as written.

placeholders.name: the name of a background process of the app, such as rms-ls or rmsd (a program name; shown as written)

workbench.native.stopped.meaning: Output headline when a background process of the app stopped unexpectedly (a restart button appears in the bottom panel). Keep {name} as written.

placeholders.name: the name of a background process of the app, such as rms-ls or rmsd (a program name; shown as written)

workbench.map-test.report-imported.meaning: Output note after File > Import Test Report… opened a saved map-test report (the results of a script that generates many maps and checks them).

placeholders.name: the file name of the map test the report belongs to, such as arabia.rmstest

workbench.map-test.import-failed.message: The map-test report could not be imported
workbench.map-test.import-failed.meaning: Output headline when File > Import Test Report… could not read the chosen map-test report.

workbench.map-test.report-exported.meaning: Output note after the Test Results panel saved its map-test report to a file.

workbench.map-test.export-failed.message: The map-test report could not be exported
workbench.map-test.export-failed.meaning: Output headline when saving the map-test report from the Test Results panel failed.

workbench.map-test.replayed.message: Replayed the finding with its recorded seed
workbench.map-test.replayed.meaning: Output note after a finding of a map test was generated again in the preview with the seed (random number start value) the test recorded for it.

workbench.map-test.replayed-with-seed.message: Replayed the finding with its recorded seed {seed}
workbench.map-test.replayed-with-seed.meaning: Output note after a finding of a map test was generated again in the preview with the seed (random number start value) the test recorded for it, naming the seed.

placeholders.seed: the seed number, shown as written, such as 1234567

workbench.game-folder.unlink-failed.message: The game folder could not be unlinked
workbench.game-folder.unlink-failed.meaning: Output headline when File > Unlink Game Folder failed (the app stays linked to the Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition game folder).

code-editor.panel.label.meaning: Accessible name of the code editor panel where random map scripts (RMS) are written. Keep "RMS" as written.

code-editor.tabs.label.meaning: Accessible name of the row of editor tabs, one per open file.

code-editor.tabs.scroll-left.meaning: Accessible name of the arrow button that scrolls the row of editor tabs to the left when not all tabs fit.

code-editor.tabs.scroll-right.meaning: Accessible name of the arrow button that scrolls the row of editor tabs to the right when not all tabs fit.

code-editor.tab.close.meaning: Accessible name of the close button on an editor tab.

placeholders.name: the file name shown on the tab, such as Arabia.rms

code-editor.tab.unsaved.meaning: Accessible name of the dot on an editor tab whose file has changes not yet saved, and the tab's accessible description then.

code-editor.tab.read-only.meaning: Accessible description of an editor tab whose file cannot be edited (a protected game or mod file).

code-editor.tab.unsaved-read-only.meaning: Accessible description of an editor tab whose file is protected and has changes not yet saved: both states, in this order.

code-editor.tab-menu.deploy.meaning: Item of the editor tabs' context menu that opens the panel to install the script as a local mod of the game. Keep the ellipsis: it opens a panel.

code-editor.tab-menu.save.meaning: Item of the editor tabs' context menu that saves the active file.

code-editor.tab-menu.clone-save-as.meaning: Item of the editor tabs' context menu for a protected (read-only) game or mod file: saves a copy under a new name. Keep the ellipsis: it opens a save dialog.

code-editor.tab-menu.save-as.meaning: Item of the editor tabs' context menu that saves the active file under a new name. Keep the ellipsis: it opens a save dialog.

code-editor.tab-menu.close.meaning: Item of the editor tabs' context menu that closes the active tab.

code-editor.run.preview.meaning: Accessible name of the Run button above the editor: generates the map of the script in the live preview.

code-editor.run.map-test.meaning: Accessible name of the Run button above the editor when a map test is open (a script that generates many maps and checks them).

code-editor.run.preview-and-live-test.meaning: Accessible name of the Run button when Live test on run is on: generates the preview, then starts the map in the running game.

code-editor.run.stop.meaning: Accessible name of the Run button while a run is in progress: stops it.

code-editor.run.tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the Run button above the editor, with its keyboard shortcut.

placeholders.shortcut: the keyboard shortcut, such as F5 (shown as written)

code-editor.run.preview-and-live-test-to.meaning: Tooltip of the Run button when Live test on run is on (it generates the preview, then starts the map in the running game), with its keyboard shortcut.

placeholders.shortcut: the keyboard shortcut, such as F5 (shown as written)

code-editor.run.stop-tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the Run button while a run is in progress (it stops the run), with its keyboard shortcut.

placeholders.shortcut: the keyboard shortcut, such as Shift+F5 (shown as written)

code-editor.run-menu.label.meaning: Accessible name of the arrow button beside Run that opens the run options menu (seed, pinned script, live test).

code-editor.run-menu.executed-script.meaning: Accessible name of the run options field that shows which script a run generates (the active one, or the pinned one).

code-editor.run-menu.pin.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the pin toggle in the run options: keeps running the current script even when another tab is active.

code-editor.run-menu.seed.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the seed field in the run options: the number that starts the random choices of map generation.

code-editor.run-menu.copy-seed.meaning: Tooltip of the seed field when its seed can be copied (its copy button copies it to the clipboard).

code-editor.run-menu.copy-seed-label.meaning: Accessible name of the button that copies the run's seed to the clipboard.

placeholders.seed: the seed number, shown as written, such as 1234567

code-editor.run-menu.seed-copied.meaning: Accessible name of the seed copy button for a moment after the seed was copied to the clipboard.

code-editor.run-menu.seed-locked.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the seed mode toggle while it keeps the seed the same for every run.

code-editor.run-menu.seed-randomize.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the seed mode toggle while every run picks a new random seed.

code-editor.run-menu.adopt-seed.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the button that copies the seed of the match running in the game (through AoE2Control) into the seed field.

code-editor.run-menu.adopt-seed-required.message: A verified active single-player random-map match is required.
code-editor.run-menu.adopt-seed-required.meaning: Tooltip of the Use current match seed button when no suitable match runs in the game: says what must run to take its seed.

code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.select.message: Select the Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition game folder
code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.select.meaning: Tooltip of the run options button that links the game folder (needed for live tests). Keep the product name as written.

code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.selecti.message: Selecting the Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition game folder
code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.selecti.meaning: Tooltip of the game folder button while the folder picker is open. Keep the product name as written.

code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.looking.message: Looking for an installed Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition game folder
code-editor.run-menu.game-folder.looking.meaning: Tooltip of the game folder button while the app searches the computer for the installed game. Keep the product name as written.

code-editor.run-menu.live-test-on-run.meaning: Toggle in the run options: each run also starts the map in the running game (a live test through AoE2Control).

code-editor.run-menu.live-test-on-run.to.message: Run the preview, then continue in AoE2DE
code-editor.run-menu.live-test-on-run.to.meaning: Tooltip of the Live test on run toggle: a run generates the preview and then starts the map in the game. Keep "AoE2DE" (the game's short name) as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.invalid.meaning: Tooltip of the disabled Live test on run toggle when the selected AoE2Control program cannot be used. Keep "AoE2Control" (a program name) as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.select.meaning: Button in the run options that picks the AoE2Control program used for live tests. Keep "AoE2Control" as written. This default button label has no trailing ellipsis, although it opens a file dialog.

code-editor.run-menu.control.selecting.meaning: The Select AoE2Control button while its file dialog is open. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.select-tool.meaning: Tooltip of the Select AoE2Control button. Keep the file name "AoE2Control.exe" as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.selecting-t.meaning: Tooltip of the Select AoE2Control button while its file dialog is open. Keep the file name "AoE2Control.exe" as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.download.meaning: Accessible name of the button that opens the AoE2Control releases page in the browser. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.run-menu.control.releases.meaning: Tooltip of the download button: opens the web page where AoE2Control is downloaded. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.control.remove.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation before the app forgets the selected AoE2Control program. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.control.remove.description.message: This removes the selected AoE2Control executable and disconnects the current live-test session. The next live test asks again before it replaces a running match.
code-editor.control.remove.description.meaning: Text of the confirmation before the app forgets the selected AoE2Control program. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.control.remove.confirm.meaning: Button of the confirmation that forgets the selected AoE2Control program.

code-editor.control.releases-failed.message: The AoE2Control releases page could not be opened
code-editor.control.releases-failed.meaning: Output headline when the browser could not be opened at the AoE2Control download page. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.control-download.title.meaning: Title of the notice shown after the AoE2Control download page opened, before the user extracts the downloaded archive. Keep "AoE2Control" as written.

code-editor.control-download.description.message: The extraction password for AoE2Control.zip is {password}. Because AoE2Control injects a DLL to run Lua in the game, heuristic antivirus tools—including Windows Defender—may flag it as a false positive. Add an antivirus folder exception for the extracted files so the engine can run without interruption.
code-editor.control-download.description.meaning: Text of the notice before extracting the downloaded AoE2Control archive: its password, and why antivirus tools may warn about it. Keep "AoE2Control.zip", "AoE2Control", "DLL", "Lua", and "Windows Defender" as written.

placeholders.password: the archive password, shown in bold and never translated (it is "control")

code-editor.control-download.confirm.meaning: Button that closes the notice before extracting AoE2Control.

code-editor.preview.collapse.meaning: Accessible name of the button above the editor that hides the live map preview beside it.

code-editor.preview.expand.meaning: Accessible name of the button above the editor that shows the live map preview again.

code-editor.preview.collapse-tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the button that hides the live map preview. "Preview" is the panel's name.

code-editor.preview.expand-tooltip.meaning: Tooltip of the button that shows the live map preview again. "Preview" is the panel's name.

code-editor.notice.execution-failure.dis.meaning: Accessible name of the close button on the floating notice that says a run of the script failed.

code-editor.notice.recovery.meaning: Floating notice at startup when the app restored changes that were not saved before it closed.

code-editor.notice.recovery.dismiss.meaning: Accessible name of the close button on the Unsaved work recovered notice.

code-editor.notice.game-textures.message: The preview now uses your game's textures
code-editor.notice.game-textures.meaning: Floating notice after the game folder was first linked: the map preview switched to drawing the map with the textures of the user's own installed game.

code-editor.font-size.label.meaning: Accessible name of the indicator that briefly shows the editor's zoom after Ctrl+mouse wheel or a zoom key.

code-editor.font-size.value.meaning: The editor's zoom as a percentage of its normal font size, shown briefly after zooming. Write the percent sign as your language does.

placeholders.percent: the zoom in percent, a whole number such as 120

code-editor.read-only-message.message: This installation or subscribed-mod source is protected. Use Clone or Save As.
code-editor.read-only-message.meaning: Message the editor shows when the user types in a protected (read-only) game or subscribed-mod file. "Clone" and "Save As" name the context-menu items that save a copy.

code-editor.context-menu.open-included-f.meaning: Item of the editor's context menu, shown while the caret is on the file name of an include line (such as #include): opens that file.

code-editor.include.open.meaning: Link at the top of the hover over an include line's file name: opens the included file.

placeholders.name: the included file's name, such as F_seasons.inc (shown as written)

code-editor.rename.unsafe.message: Rename is not semantically safe here.
code-editor.rename.unsafe.meaning: Shown when Rename Symbol cannot rename the name at the caret, because the result could change what the script means.

code-editor.rename.not-proven.meaning: Shown when Rename Symbol refused a rename: the app could not prove the renamed script means the same as before.

code-editor.rename.protected-file.message: {name} is a protected game file; the rename would change it.
code-editor.rename.protected-file.meaning: Shown when Rename Symbol refused a rename because it would also edit a read-only game file that uses the name.

placeholders.name: the protected file's name, such as random_map.def

code-editor.quick-fix.ignore-on-line.meaning: Quick fix offered for a lint warning: adds a comment that silences that warning on this line only. Keep {code} as written.

placeholders.code: the lint rule's code, such as RMS4001

code-editor.quick-fix.turn-off-rule.meaning: Quick fix offered for a lint warning: turns that lint rule off for every script of the open folder (View > Lint Rules turns it on again). Keep {code} as written.

placeholders.code: the lint rule's code, such as RMS4001

code-editor.format.reason.model-unavaila.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing: the file's editor was closed meanwhile.

code-editor.format.reason.language-chang.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing: the file became another kind of script (for example .rms renamed to .xs) meanwhile.

code-editor.format.reason.changed-before.message: The document changed before formatting began.
code-editor.format.reason.changed-before.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing: the file was edited before formatting started.

code-editor.format.reason.changed-while-.message: The document changed while formatting was pending.
code-editor.format.reason.changed-while-.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing: the file was edited while formatting was being prepared.

code-editor.format.reason.cancelled.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing: formatting was cancelled.

code-editor.format.reason.starlark-inval.message: Formatting is unavailable while the Starlark source is invalid.
code-editor.format.reason.starlark-inval.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing for a map test (a script in the Starlark language): the script has errors. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.format.reason.starlark-inden.message: Formatting requires already-valid four-space indentation; token structure was left unchanged.
code-editor.format.reason.starlark-inden.meaning: Why Format Document did nothing for a map test (a Starlark script): its lines must already be indented in steps of four spaces; the script was not changed.

code-editor.completion.content.object.meaning: Detail beside a suggested object constant whose name the linked game does not give: the object's number. Lower case, a short label.

placeholders.id: the object's number in the game data, shown as written, such as 1981

code-editor.completion.content.terrain.meaning: Detail beside a suggested terrain constant whose name the linked game does not give: the terrain's number. Lower case, a short label.

placeholders.id: the terrain's number in the game data, shown as written, such as 54

code-editor.completion.content.named.meaning: Detail beside a suggested object or terrain constant: its name in the linked game, then its number.

placeholders.name: the name the linked game gives the object or terrain (in the game's language), such as Gold Mine
placeholders.id: its number in the game data, shown as written, such as 66

code-editor.completion.map-test.meaning: Detail beside a suggestion that belongs to the map-test functions (rms, rms.generate, sample.expect, …) in a map test script.

code-editor.completion.starlark-built-in.meaning: Detail beside a suggested built-in function of the Starlark language (len, range, …) in a map test script. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.completion.starlark-method.meaning: Detail beside a suggested method of a Starlark value (such as split of a string). Keep "Starlark" and {type} as written.

placeholders.type: the Starlark type name, shown as written: string, list, or dict

code-editor.completion.starlark-function.meaning: Detail beside a suggested function the map test script defined earlier. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.completion.starlark-paramete.meaning: Detail beside a suggested parameter of the function the caret is in. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.completion.starlark-variable.meaning: Detail beside a suggested variable the map test script assigned earlier. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.completion.starlark-loop-var.meaning: Detail beside a suggested variable of a for loop. Keep "Starlark" as written.

code-editor.completion.defined-earlier.message: {name} was defined earlier in this document.
code-editor.completion.defined-earlier.meaning: Documentation of a suggested function or variable that the map test script defined earlier.

placeholders.name: the function or variable name, such as gold_count (shown as written)

code-editor.symbol.starlark-function.meaning: Detail beside a function of a map test script in Go to Symbol (the list of the script's functions). Keep "Starlark" as written.

native-dialog.source-files.filter.meaning: File type name in the Windows Open and Save As dialogs for script files (.rms, .rms2, .inc, .def, .xs). RMS and XS are script kinds and stay as written.

native-dialog.source-files.filter.map-te.meaning: File type name in the Windows Open and Save As dialogs for script files, including map-test scripts (.rmstest). RMS and XS are script kinds and stay as written.

native-dialog.open-files.title.meaning: Title of the Windows Open dialog that opens one or more script files in the editor.

native-dialog.open-folder.title.meaning: Title of the Windows folder dialog that opens a folder of random map scripts as the workspace. RMS stays as written.

native-dialog.save-as.title.meaning: Title of the Windows Save As dialog for a script file.

native-dialog.map-test-report.filter.meaning: File type name in the Windows dialogs that export or import a map-test report (a .json file with the results of a map test).

native-dialog.map-test-report.export.tit.meaning: Title of the Windows Save dialog that exports the results of a map test as a report file.

native-dialog.map-test-report.import.tit.meaning: Title of the Windows Open dialog that imports a map-test report file to show its results.

native-dialog.game-folder.title.message: Select an Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition folder
native-dialog.game-folder.title.meaning: Title of the Windows folder dialog where the user picks the installation folder of the game to link it. The game name Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition stays as written.

native-dialog.installed-map-clone.title.message: Select a parent folder for the editable map clone
native-dialog.installed-map-clone.title.meaning: Title of the Windows folder dialog where the user picks the folder in which an editable copy of an installed map (and the files it includes) is created.

native-dialog.control-launcher.title.meaning: Title of the Windows Open dialog where the user picks the AoE2Control program used for live tests. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

native-dialog.control-launcher.filter.meaning: File type name (.exe programs) in the Windows Open dialog for AoE2Control. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

native-dialog.map-icon.title.meaning: Title of the Windows Save dialog that saves the map's icon image as a PNG file.

native-dialog.map-icon.filter.meaning: File type name in the Windows Save dialog for a map icon. PNG is the image format and stays as written.

file-actions.included-files.refresh-fail.message: Included files could not be refreshed
file-actions.included-files.refresh-fail.meaning: Main-owned Output warning headline when the current generation dependency graph could not be prepared or validated. Current graph proof is unavailable; stale contents do not retain analysis, cache or deployment authority. Independent editor assistance has its own warning.

file-actions.delete.session-not-updated.message: The session could not be updated after the delete
file-actions.delete.session-not-updated.meaning: Output warning headline: a file or folder was deleted from the Explorer, but the saved list of open tabs and folders (the session) could not be updated afterwards.

file-actions.explorer.folders-unreadable.message: Some folders could not be shown in the Explorer
file-actions.explorer.folders-unreadable.meaning: Output warning headline: some folders of the workspace could not be read, so the Explorer (the file tree on the left) leaves them out.

file-actions.standard-resource-conflict.message: {count, plural, one {A workspace file has the name of a game library file} other {Workspace files have the names of game library files}}
file-actions.standard-resource-conflict.meaning: Output warning headline: files in the open folder have the same names as library files the game ships (such as random_map.def), so an include may read the game's file instead.

placeholders.count: how many workspace files have such a name

file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..message: {paths, list, unit}. They stay editable, but includes may pick the game's file instead.
file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..meaning: Cause line of the warning about workspace files named like game library files: first the files, then why it matters.

placeholders.paths: the workspace files with such names, as paths, shown as written and joined without a conjunction

file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..message: {count, plural, other {{paths, list, unit}, and {count} more. They stay editable, but includes may pick the game's file instead.}}
file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..meaning: Cause line of the warning about workspace files named like game library files, when there are more than eight: the first eight files, how many more, then why it matters.

placeholders.paths: the first eight workspace files with such names, as paths, shown as written and joined without a conjunction
placeholders.count: how many more files have such names

file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..meaning: Action of the warning about workspace files named like game library files: rename those files.

file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..message: The check for game library file names was incomplete
file-actions.standard-resource-conflict..meaning: Output warning headline: the IDE could not finish checking whether workspace files have the names of library files the game ships.

file-actions.shell-open.refused.meaning: Output warning headline: Windows asked AoE2RMSIDE to open files or folders (a double-click or the command line), but the request was refused as a whole.

file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-many.message: {count, plural, other {The request named more than {count} files and folders.}}
file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-many.meaning: Cause when Windows asked to open too many files and folders at once.

placeholders.count: the most files and folders one request may name, such as 64

file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-long.message: The request’s paths are longer than AoE2RMSIDE accepts.
file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-long.meaning: Cause when the file paths Windows asked to open are too long. AoE2RMSIDE is the product name and stays as written.

file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-many.message: Too many open requests arrived at once. Open the remaining items again.
