file-actions.shell-open.refused.too-many.meaning: Cause when Windows sent more open requests at once than the app queues; the user opens the rest again.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.meaning: Output warning headline: one file or folder Windows asked to open was not opened.

placeholders.name: the file or folder name, such as Arabia.rms

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.missing.message: It does not exist or cannot be reached.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.missing.meaning: Cause: the file or folder Windows asked to open does not exist or cannot be reached.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.invalid.message: It is not a valid file or folder path.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.invalid.meaning: Cause: what Windows asked to open is not a valid path.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.unsuppo.message: AoE2RMSIDE opens folders and .rms, .rms2, .inc, .def, and .xs files.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.unsuppo.meaning: Cause: the file Windows asked to open is not a kind the app opens. AoE2RMSIDE and the file extensions stay as written.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.unsuppo.message: AoE2RMSIDE opens folders and .rms, .rms2, .inc, .def, .xs, and .rmstest files.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.unsuppo.meaning: Cause: the file Windows asked to open is not a kind the app opens (in the edition that also opens map-test scripts, .rmstest). AoE2RMSIDE and the file extensions stay as written.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.second-.message: One folder opens at a time.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.second-.meaning: Cause: Windows asked to open more than one folder; only one folder opens as the workspace.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.second-.message: One folder opens at a time; {folder} opened as the folder.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.second-.meaning: Cause: Windows asked to open more than one folder; only one opens as the workspace, and this names the one that opened.

placeholders.folder: the name of the folder that opened, such as Maps

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.unreada.meaning: Cause: the file Windows asked to open could not be read.

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.more.message: {count, plural, one {# more item was not opened} other {# more items were not opened}}
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.more.meaning: Output warning headline after the first rejected items are listed one by one: how many more files or folders were not opened.

placeholders.count: how many more items were not opened

file-actions.shell-open.rejected.more.ca.message: They do not exist, cannot be read, or are not files AoE2RMSIDE opens.
file-actions.shell-open.rejected.more.ca.meaning: Cause of the count of further items that were not opened. AoE2RMSIDE is the product name and stays as written.

file-actions.entry.name-exists.message: an entry with that name already exists
file-actions.entry.name-exists.meaning: Says a file or folder with this name is already in the folder. Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.name-or-alias-exists.message: an entry with that name, or a short-name alias of it, already exists
file-actions.entry.name-or-alias-exists.meaning: Says a file or folder with this name, or with a Windows short 8.3 name (such as MAPFIL~1.RMS) that matches it, is already in the folder. Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.invalid-name.message: name is not a valid Windows basename
file-actions.entry.invalid-name.meaning: Says the name cannot be used as a Windows file or folder name (empty, reserved such as CON, a forbidden character such as : or ?, or ending in a dot or space). Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.unsupported-kind.message: only .rms, .rms2, .inc, .def, and .xs source files are supported
file-actions.entry.unsupported-kind.meaning: Says the IDE creates and opens only script files with these extensions, which stay as written. Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.unsupported-kind.map-.message: only .rms, .rms2, .inc, .def, .rmstest, and .xs source files are supported
file-actions.entry.unsupported-kind.map-.meaning: Says the IDE creates and opens only script files with these extensions (in the edition that also has map-test scripts, .rmstest), which stay as written. Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.read-only.message: workspace entry is read-only or protected
file-actions.entry.read-only.meaning: Says this file or folder cannot be changed: it is read-only or the IDE protects it (such as a deployed mod folder). Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.root-locked.message: workspace root cannot be renamed or deleted
file-actions.entry.root-locked.meaning: Says the open workspace folder itself (the top of the Explorer tree) cannot be renamed or deleted from the Explorer. Explorer inline error under the name box while creating or renaming a file or folder (it may also appear in Output). It is shown as written, lower case and without a full stop, like the other short inline errors.

file-actions.entry.reserved-name.message: ''{name}'' is reserved for a standard game resource; choose a different filename.
file-actions.entry.reserved-name.meaning: Says the name belongs to a library file the game ships (such as random_map.def), so a script file of that name would hide it; the user picks another name. Shown in the Explorer's inline name error and in Output messages of deployments and installed-map copies. Keep the quotes around the name. The doubled apostrophes stand for one straight apostrophe each (message format quoting).

placeholders.name: the file name the user entered, such as random_map.def

notice.recovery.read-failed.message: Unsaved work from the last session could not be read and was skipped
notice.recovery.read-failed.meaning: Output warning headline at startup: the unsaved changes kept from the last session (after a crash or restart) could not be read, so they were not restored.

notice.recovery.folder-unavailable.message: The recovered workspace folder is unavailable.
notice.recovery.folder-unavailable.meaning: Output warning at startup: the folder that was open before the app closed unexpectedly cannot be reached, so it was not opened again.

notice.recovery.previous-folder-skipped.message: The previous workspace folder is unavailable and was skipped.
notice.recovery.previous-folder-skipped.meaning: Output warning at startup: the folder open in the last session cannot be reached, so it was not opened again.

notice.recovery.tab-skipped.meaning: Output warning at startup: a file open as a tab in the last session cannot be reached or read, so its tab was not opened again.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

notice.recovery.recovered-unsaved.message: Recovered {name} as an unsaved buffer because its source is unavailable.
notice.recovery.recovered-unsaved.meaning: Output warning at startup: unsaved changes to a file were restored, but the file itself cannot be reached, so they open in a new unsaved tab.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

notice.game-textures.terrain-ready.message: {reused, plural, other {{converted} converted and {reused} reused terrain files from the linked game in {seconds, number, ::.0 group-off} s}}
notice.game-textures.terrain-ready.meaning: Output headline when the Game textures look is ready: how many terrain image files were newly converted from the user's linked game and how many were reused from the local cache, and how long it took in seconds (s).

placeholders.converted: how many terrain files were converted now
placeholders.reused: how many terrain files were reused from the local cache
placeholders.seconds: how long it took, in seconds with one decimal

notice.game-textures.terrain-ready.cause.meaning: Cause line when the Game textures look is ready: the size of the converted textures kept on this computer.

placeholders.megabytes: the size of the local cache, in megabytes with one decimal

notice.game-textures.terrain-fallback.message: {count, plural, other {{count} terrain files could not be converted and use minimap colors}}
notice.game-textures.terrain-fallback.meaning: Output warning headline: some terrain image files of the linked game could not be converted, so those terrains are drawn in their plain minimap colors.

placeholders.count: how many terrain files could not be converted

notice.game-textures.terrain-fallback.ca.meaning: Cause line of the warning about terrain files that could not be converted: one of them and why.

placeholders.asset: the game's file name of one terrain image, as written
placeholders.reason: why it could not be converted, in English as the converter reports it

preview-panel.name.object-number.meaning: Name of a map object that has no name, shown in the map preview's legend, selection list, and tooltips: the word for a game object followed by its numeric identity.

placeholders.id: the object's numeric identity, such as 66, or several identities joined by commas, such as 66, 67

preview-panel.name.terrain-number.meaning: Name of a terrain that has no name, shown in the map preview's legend, selection list, and tooltips: the word for a terrain type followed by its numeric identity.

placeholders.id: the terrain's numeric identity, such as 12, or several identities joined by commas

preview-panel.name.with-constant.meaning: An object or terrain name read from the user's linked game installation, followed by the RMS constant scripts use for it, as in Town Center (TOWN_CENTER). Shown in the map preview's legend, selection list, and tooltips. Keep both placeholders; only the punctuation around the constant may change.

placeholders.name: the object or terrain name in the game's own words, such as Town Center
placeholders.constant: the RMS constant, such as TOWN_CENTER; stays as written

preview-panel.name.wall-number.meaning: Name of a wall object that has no name, shown in the map preview's legend and selection list: the word for a wall followed by its numeric identity.

placeholders.id: the wall object's numeric identity, such as 72, or several identities joined by commas

preview-panel.material.owner-short.meaning: Short muted suffix after an object's name in a legend row, naming the player who owns it (P2 = player 2). Keep it as short as possible.

preview-panel.material.player.meaning: Tooltip detail of a legend row: the player who owns the object.

preview-panel.material.gaia.meaning: Tooltip detail of a legend row: the object belongs to no player (nature, the neutral side the game calls Gaia). Use the game's own word for it.

preview-panel.material.helper-object.meaning: Tooltip detail of a legend row: the object is a helper that is invisible in the game (for example a terrain blocker), shown by the preview only on request.

preview-panel.material.cliff.meaning: Name of a legend row for cliffs on the map.

preview-panel.material.cliff-type.meaning: Tooltip detail of a cliff legend row: which cliff type it is, by number.

placeholders.id: the cliff type's number, such as 0, or several joined by commas

preview-panel.material.connection.land.meaning: Name of the legend row for a land connection drawn between areas (a path the generator connects over land) in the map preview.

preview-panel.material.connection.water.meaning: Name of the legend row for a water connection drawn between areas in the map preview.

preview-panel.material.connection.road.meaning: Name of the legend row for a road connection drawn between areas in the map preview.

preview-panel.material.connection.unknow.meaning: Name of the legend row for a connection between areas whose kind is not known in the map preview.

preview-panel.material.connection.failed.meaning: Name of the legend row for a connection search between two areas that found no path (drawn as a thin dashed line while the map preview shows traced connection paths).

preview-panel.material.description.meaning: A legend row's full description, used as its accessible name, in its tooltip, and in Output: its name followed by its details in parentheses, as in Town Center (Object 109, Player 2).

placeholders.name: the row's name, such as Town Center or Object 66
placeholders.details: the row's details, such as Object 109 and Player 2, joined as a list without a conjunction

preview-panel.material.selection-ambigui.message: Preview selection ambiguity: {layer} · {count, plural, one {{count} selected} other {{count} selected}} · {sources, plural, one {{sources} distinct source} other {{sources} distinct sources}} · using {location}.
preview-panel.material.selection-ambigui.meaning: Output note when one legend row stands for map items placed by several script commands: it names the row, how many items are selected, how many different script places placed them, and the one place the editor reveals.

placeholders.layer: the legend row's description, such as Gold Mine (Object 66, Gaia)
placeholders.count: how many items the row selects, 2 or more
placeholders.sources: how many different script commands placed them, 2 or more
placeholders.location: the revealed script place: a file and a byte range, such as Arabia.rms:120-160; stays as written

preview-panel.material.terrain.grass.meaning: The app's own name for grass, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.shallows.meaning: The app's own name for shallow water, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.water.meaning: The app's own name for water, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.beach.meaning: The app's own name for beach, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.earth.meaning: The app's own name for earth (bare ground), shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.stone.meaning: The app's own name for stone ground, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.dirt.meaning: The app's own name for dirt, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.material.terrain.cliff-fac.meaning: The app's own name for the terrain under a cliff face, shown in the map preview's legend and selection rows when no game name is known for the terrain. A short terrain name.

preview-panel.candidate.stage.land.meaning: The stage the map generator is working on while the preview draws the map as it is generated: placing the land areas. Shown inside a longer status such as "Generating · Land".

preview-panel.candidate.stage.elevation.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: raising hills (elevation).

preview-panel.candidate.stage.cliffs.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: placing cliffs.

preview-panel.candidate.stage.terrain.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: painting terrains (grass, water, forest ground).

preview-panel.candidate.stage.connection.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: drawing connections (roads and paths between areas).

preview-panel.candidate.stage.objects.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: placing objects (units, resources, buildings).

preview-panel.candidate.stage.finished.meaning: Generation stage shown while the preview draws the map as it is generated: the map is finished.

preview-panel.candidate.generating.meaning: Status over the map preview while a map is being generated and drawn step by step. The dot separates the two parts.

placeholders.stage: the current generation stage, such as Land or Objects

preview-panel.candidate.sample-stage.meaning: Status over the map preview while one map of a batch of sample maps is generated. A seed is the number that makes a random map repeatable.

placeholders.sample: the sample map's number in the batch, starting at 1
placeholders.seed: the map's seed number, shown as the engine wrote it
placeholders.stage: the current generation stage, such as Land or Objects

preview-panel.candidate.sample-finished.meaning: Status over the map preview when one sample map of a batch is finished and the other sample maps are still being generated. A seed is the number that makes a random map repeatable.

placeholders.sample: the sample map's number in the batch, starting at 1
placeholders.seed: the map's seed number, shown as the engine wrote it

preview-panel.keyboard.help.message: Arrow keys select a tile, Shift+Arrow extends the selection, Ctrl+Arrow pans, plus and minus zoom, 0 fits the map, Ctrl+A selects the whole map, Escape clears the selection.
preview-panel.keyboard.help.meaning: Hidden help read by screen readers when the map canvas has focus: lists its keyboard shortcuts. Keep the key names Arrow, Shift, Ctrl, A, 0, and Escape as the keys are labelled on a keyboard.

preview-panel.selection.announce.cleared.meaning: Announced to screen readers when the tile selection on the map is cleared.

preview-panel.selection.announce.tile.meaning: Announced to screen readers when one map tile is selected: its coordinates.

preview-panel.selection.announce.tiles.message: Tiles {fromX}, {fromY} to {toX}, {toY}, {count, plural, one {{count} tile} other {{count} tiles}}
preview-panel.selection.announce.tiles.meaning: Announced to screen readers when a rectangle of map tiles is selected: its corner coordinates and how many tiles it covers.

placeholders.fromX: the x coordinate of the first corner
placeholders.fromY: the y coordinate of the first corner
placeholders.toX: the x coordinate of the opposite corner
placeholders.toY: the y coordinate of the opposite corner
placeholders.count: how many tiles are selected (always two or more)

preview-panel.selection.announce.no-laye.meaning: Announced to screen readers after a selection when nothing is on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.selection.announce.layer.meaning: One entry of the screen-reader announcement of what is on the selected tiles: a terrain or object and how many there are, such as "Grass 4".

placeholders.name: the terrain or object, such as Grass or Gold Mine
placeholders.count: how many tiles or objects of it are selected

preview-panel.selection.announce.layers.message: {area}. {count, plural, one {{count} layer} other {{count} layers}}: {shown, list, unit}
preview-panel.selection.announce.layers.meaning: Announced to screen readers after a selection: the selected tiles and what is on them (terrains and objects, here called layers).

placeholders.count: how many layers are on the selected tiles (three or fewer)
placeholders.shown: the layers with their counts, such as "Grass 4"

preview-panel.selection.announce.layers-.message: {area}. {count, plural, one {{count} layer} other {{count} layers}}: {shown, list, unit}, and {more} more
preview-panel.selection.announce.layers-.meaning: Announced to screen readers after a selection: the selected tiles, the first three of what is on them (terrains and objects, here called layers), and how many more there are.

placeholders.count: how many layers are on the selected tiles (more than three)
placeholders.shown: the first three layers with their counts, such as "Grass 4"
placeholders.more: how many layers are not named

preview-panel.run.include-only.message: .inc, .def and .xs documents are include-only and cannot be run.
preview-panel.run.include-only.meaning: Why Run is unavailable for the open document: files ending in .inc, .def, or .xs are only included by a map script and cannot be generated on their own. Keep .inc, .def, and .xs as written.

preview-panel.tool.objects.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar: shows or hides the objects on the map and the Town Center's footprint. Use the game's own name for the Town Center building.

preview-panel.tool.cliffs.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar: shows or hides the cliff edges.

preview-panel.tool.connection-terrain.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar: shows or hides the terrain that connections (roads and paths between areas) painted.

preview-panel.tool.connections.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the connection button in the map preview toolbar, which cycles how connections (roads and paths between areas) are drawn; this state draws a straight line between the two ends of each connection.

preview-panel.tool.connections.off.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the connection button in the map preview toolbar, which cycles how connections (roads and paths between areas) are drawn; this state draws none of them. The next states are Connection lines and Traced connection paths.

preview-panel.tool.connections.paths.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of the connection button in the map preview toolbar, which cycles how connections (roads and paths between areas) are drawn; this state draws, for each connection, the line of tiles the map generator's search actually went through, and the searches that found no path as thin dashed lines.

preview-panel.tool.connections.paths-par.meaning: Second tooltip line of the connection button while it draws traced connection paths and not every path search of the map is drawn: the map generator keeps the first searches only, so a map with many connections shows some of them. Paths counts searches, including those that found no path.

placeholders.shown: how many path searches are drawn, such as 2,048
placeholders.total: how many path searches the map generator ran, such as 3,100

preview-panel.tool.connections.paths-not.message: Traced paths show once the map is finished
preview-panel.tool.connections.paths-not.meaning: Second tooltip line of the connection button while a map is still being generated (an intermediate stage or the previous map is shown): its cycle then skips the traced connection paths state, which needs the finished map.

preview-panel.tool.connections.paths-una.message: Traced paths are not available for this map
preview-panel.tool.connections.paths-una.meaning: Second tooltip line of the connection button when the shown map has no traced connection paths (for example a map shown from a map test): its cycle then skips the traced connection paths state.

preview-panel.tool.elevation.off.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles how hills are drawn; this state draws no elevation.

preview-panel.tool.elevation.terrain.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles how hills are drawn; this state shades the terrain by its height.

preview-panel.tool.elevation.height-map.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles how hills are drawn; this state colors each tile by its height.

preview-panel.tool.perspective.top-down.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that switches the perspective; this state shows the map seen straight from above.

preview-panel.tool.perspective.diamond.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that switches the perspective; this state shows the map as a diamond, like the in-game minimap.

preview-panel.tool.look.minimap.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles the look of the map; this state draws each tile in the game's minimap colors.

preview-panel.tool.look.texture-colors.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles the look of the map; this state draws each tile in one color taken from its terrain texture.

preview-panel.tool.look.game-textures.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar that cycles the look of the map; this state draws the map with the art of the user's own linked game.

preview-panel.tool.look.applying.meaning: Tooltip of the Look button while the art of the user's own linked game is being applied to the shown map.

preview-panel.tool.tile-grid.meaning: Accessible name and tooltip of an icon button in the map preview toolbar: shows or hides a grid of the map tiles.

preview-panel.canvas.top-down.minimap.message: top-down map preview in minimap colors
preview-panel.canvas.top-down.minimap.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map seen from above, drawn in the game's minimap colors. Lower case, as screen readers read it after the role.

preview-panel.canvas.top-down.texture-co.message: top-down map preview in texture colors
preview-panel.canvas.top-down.texture-co.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map seen from above, drawn in one color per terrain texture. Lower case, as screen readers read it after the role.

preview-panel.canvas.top-down.game-textu.message: top-down map preview with game textures
preview-panel.canvas.top-down.game-textu.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map seen from above, drawn with the art of the user's own linked game. Lower case, as screen readers read it after the role.

preview-panel.canvas.diamond.minimap.message: 2-to-1 diamond map preview in minimap colors
preview-panel.canvas.diamond.minimap.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map as a diamond twice as wide as high (like the in-game minimap), drawn in the game's minimap colors.

preview-panel.canvas.diamond.texture-col.message: 2-to-1 diamond map preview in texture colors
preview-panel.canvas.diamond.texture-col.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map as a diamond twice as wide as high (like the in-game minimap), drawn in one color per terrain texture.

preview-panel.canvas.diamond.game-textur.message: 2-to-1 diamond map preview with game textures
preview-panel.canvas.diamond.game-textur.meaning: Accessible name of the map canvas in the preview: the map as a diamond twice as wide as high (like the in-game minimap), drawn with the art of the user's own linked game.

preview-panel.canvas.role-description.meaning: What screen readers call the map canvas (its role), in lower case: a map the keyboard can move around in.

preview-panel.announce.ready.meaning: Announced to screen readers when the first generated map is shown.

preview-panel.announce.updated.meaning: Announced to screen readers when a newly generated map replaces the shown one.

preview-panel.panel.label.meaning: Accessible name of the map preview panel, which shows the map the script generates.

preview-panel.toolbar.label.meaning: Accessible name of the toolbar of buttons over the map preview.

preview-panel.toolbar.connections.meaning: Accessible name of the group of toolbar buttons about connections (roads and paths between areas).

preview-panel.toolbar.keyboard-cue.meaning: Short hint shown after the toolbar while the map has keyboard focus.

preview-panel.readout.cursor.meaning: The map coordinates of the tile under the mouse pointer, shown in the corner of the preview. x and y are the map axes.

preview-panel.status.label.meaning: Accessible name of the hidden status region of the map preview (read by screen readers).

preview-panel.status.uncertified.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: the map comes from an internal development fixture whose output was not compared against the game.

preview-panel.status.seed.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: the seed of the map (the number that makes a random map repeatable).

placeholders.seed: the seed number, shown as the engine wrote it

preview-panel.status.revision.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: which edit of the script the map belongs to.

preview-panel.status.generation.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: the stage name used when the map generator names no stage (lower case, like the engine's stage names).

preview-panel.status.generation-progress.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: the map generator's progress, in its own words.

placeholders.stage: the generator's stage name (English engine word)
placeholders.kind: the kind of progress event (English engine word)
placeholders.total: how many there are

preview-panel.status.generation-time.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: how long generating the map took. "ms" is the unit symbol for milliseconds.

preview-panel.status.cache.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: how many maps the preview keeps for reuse and how often a kept map was reused.

placeholders.hits: how many times a kept map was reused

preview-panel.status.phase.editing.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the script is being edited.

preview-panel.status.phase.analyzing.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the script is being checked before generating.

preview-panel.status.phase.unchanged.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the edit did not change the map, so it was not generated again.

preview-panel.status.phase.invalid.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the shown map is out of date because the script has errors.

preview-panel.status.phase.generating.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the map is being generated.

preview-panel.status.phase.current.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the shown map matches the script.

preview-panel.status.phase.failed.meaning: Part of the hidden status region of the map preview, read by screen readers: what the preview is doing: the shown map is out of date because generating failed.

preview-panel.legend.label.meaning: Accessible name of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.legend.filter.label.meaning: Accessible name of the filter field of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.legend.filter.clear.meaning: Accessible name of the button that empties the filter field of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.legend.filter.placeholder.meaning: Placeholder of the filter field of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.legend.filter.empty.meaning: Shown in the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles when nothing matches the filter.

preview-panel.legend.rows.meaning: Accessible name of the list of rows of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles.

preview-panel.legend.row.provisional.meaning: Accessible name of a row of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles while the map is still being generated: the counts can still grow.

placeholders.name: the terrain or object, such as Grass or Gold Mine
placeholders.count: how many are selected so far

preview-panel.legend.row.open-source.meaning: Accessible name of a row of the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles: clicking it opens the script line that placed it.

placeholders.name: the terrain or object, such as Grass or Gold Mine
placeholders.count: how many are selected

preview-panel.legend.helpers.show.meaning: Button under the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles: also lists helper objects (objects that are not visible in the game).

placeholders.count: how many helper object rows there are

preview-panel.legend.helpers.hide.meaning: Button under the legend beside the map that lists the terrains and objects on the selected tiles: stops listing helper objects (objects that are not visible in the game).

placeholders.count: how many helper object rows there are

preview-panel.fixtures.label.meaning: Accessible name of the list of internal test maps (fixtures) the preview can show; shown only in development builds of the app, never in a release.

preview-panel.fixtures.select-placeholde.meaning: First entry of the select that runs an internal test map (fixture); shown only in development builds of the app, never in a release. Uncertified: their output was not compared against the game.

preview-panel.fixtures.heading.meaning: Heading over the buttons that run internal test maps (fixtures); shown only in development builds of the app, never in a release. Uncertified: their output was not compared against the game.

preview-panel.fixtures.run.meaning: Accessible name of a button that runs one internal test map (fixture); shown only in development builds of the app, never in a release.

game-art.progress.catalog.action.meaning: One-word label beside the progress bar while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look: it is reading the game's list of art files.

game-art.progress.catalog.detail.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar: the app reads the list of art files of the user's own installed game.

game-art.progress.catalog.detail-counted.message: Reading the game's art catalog, {percent}% ({completed} of {total} {unit, select, graphics {graphics} other {files}})
game-art.progress.catalog.detail-counted.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar with its progress: the app reads the list of art files of the user's own installed game.

placeholders.percent: how much is done, as a whole number from 0 to 100
placeholders.total: how many files there are
placeholders.unit: graphics for sprite pictures, files otherwise (choose the word in each branch)

game-art.progress.terrain.action.meaning: One-word label beside the progress bar while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look: it is importing terrain textures.

game-art.progress.terrain.detail.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar: the app imports terrain textures from the user's own installed game.

game-art.progress.terrain.detail-counted.message: Importing terrain textures, {percent}% ({completed} of {total} {unit, select, graphics {graphics} other {files}})
game-art.progress.terrain.detail-counted.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar with its progress: the app imports terrain textures from the user's own installed game.

placeholders.percent: how much is done, as a whole number from 0 to 100
placeholders.total: how many files there are
placeholders.unit: graphics for sprite pictures, files otherwise (choose the word in each branch)

game-art.progress.blends.action.meaning: One-word label beside the progress bar while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look: it is blending the transitions between terrains.

game-art.progress.blends.detail.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar: the app prepares the blended transitions between terrains.

game-art.progress.blends.detail-counted.message: Blending terrain transitions, {percent}% ({completed} of {total} {unit, select, graphics {graphics} other {files}})
game-art.progress.blends.detail-counted.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar with its progress: the app prepares the blended transitions between terrains.

placeholders.percent: how much is done, as a whole number from 0 to 100
placeholders.total: how many files there are
placeholders.unit: graphics for sprite pictures, files otherwise (choose the word in each branch)

game-art.progress.masks.action.meaning: One-word label beside the progress bar while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look: it is preparing terrain overlay masks.

game-art.progress.masks.detail.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar: the app prepares the masks that lay one terrain over another.

game-art.progress.masks.detail-counted.message: Preparing terrain overlay masks, {percent}% ({completed} of {total} {unit, select, graphics {graphics} other {files}})
game-art.progress.masks.detail-counted.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar with its progress: the app prepares the masks that lay one terrain over another.

placeholders.percent: how much is done, as a whole number from 0 to 100
placeholders.total: how many files there are
placeholders.unit: graphics for sprite pictures, files otherwise (choose the word in each branch)

game-art.progress.sprites.action.meaning: One-word label beside the progress bar while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look: it is converting the object sprites (unit and resource pictures) this map needs.

game-art.progress.sprites.detail.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar: the app converts the object sprites (unit and resource pictures) this map needs.

game-art.progress.sprites.detail-counted.message: Converting this map's object sprites, {percent}% ({completed} of {total} {unit, select, graphics {graphics} other {files}})
game-art.progress.sprites.detail-counted.meaning: Tooltip and screen-reader value of the Game textures conversion progress bar with its progress: the app converts the object sprites (unit and resource pictures) this map needs.

placeholders.percent: how much is done, as a whole number from 0 to 100
placeholders.completed: how many sprite pictures are done
placeholders.total: how many sprite pictures there are
placeholders.unit: graphics for sprite pictures, files otherwise (choose the word in each branch)

game-art.progress.label.meaning: Accessible name of the progress bar shown while the app converts the art of the user's own installed game for the Game textures look.

game-art.glyphs.message: {count, plural, one {{count} object type has no sprite from the linked game and keeps its minimap glyph: {names, list, unit}} other {{count} object types have no sprite from the linked game and keep their minimap glyphs: {names, list, unit}}}
game-art.glyphs.meaning: Output note when the Game textures look draws a map: some object types have no picture (sprite) in the user's own linked game, so the preview draws them with the small minimap symbol (glyph) instead.

placeholders.count: how many object types have no sprite (four or fewer)
placeholders.names: the object types, each such as "Gold Mine (object 66)"

game-art.glyphs.more.message: {count, plural, one {{count} object type has no sprite from the linked game and keeps its minimap glyph: {names, list, unit}, and {more} more} other {{count} object types have no sprite from the linked game and keep their minimap glyphs: {names, list, unit}, and {more} more}}
game-art.glyphs.more.meaning: Output note when the Game textures look draws a map: many object types have no picture (sprite) in the user's own linked game, so the preview draws them with the small minimap symbol (glyph) instead. The first four are named; the rest are counted.

placeholders.count: how many object types have no sprite (more than four)
placeholders.names: the first four object types, each such as "Gold Mine (object 66)"
placeholders.more: how many object types are not named

game-art.glyphs.object-named.meaning: One object type in the Output note about objects without a sprite: its name from the game and its object number.

placeholders.name: the object's name from the linked game, such as Gold Mine

game-art.glyphs.object.meaning: One object type in the Output note about objects without a sprite, when the game gives it no name: its object number.

game-art.cliff-lines.message: {count, plural, one {{count} cliff piece has no sprite from the linked game and keeps its cliff line} other {{count} cliff pieces have no sprite from the linked game and keep their cliff line}}
game-art.cliff-lines.meaning: Output note when the Game textures look draws a map: some cliff pieces have no picture (sprite) in the user's own linked game, so the preview draws them as a plain cliff line instead.

placeholders.count: how many cliff pieces have no sprite

profiler.group.parse.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): reading the script.

profiler.group.setup.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): setting up the players.

profiler.group.land.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): placing the land areas.

profiler.group.elevation.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): raising hills.

profiler.group.cliffs.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): placing cliffs.

profiler.group.terrain.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): painting terrains.

profiler.group.connections.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): drawing connections (roads and paths between areas).

profiler.group.objects.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): placing objects (units, resources, buildings).

profiler.group.finalize.meaning: Name of one phase of map generation in the execution profiler (which shows how long each phase of generating the map took): the last steps after placing objects.

profiler.step.parse-script.meaning: Name of one step of map generation in a row of the execution profiler (which lists how long each step took): reading the script.

profiler.pending.waiting.message: Waiting for the first step to complete

profiler.duration.seconds.meaning: A time in seconds with two decimals, as shown on the execution profiler button and rows. "s" is the short unit symbol for seconds.

profiler.duration.milliseconds.hundredth.meaning: A short time in milliseconds with two decimals (below 10 ms), in an execution profiler row. "ms" is the unit symbol for milliseconds.

profiler.duration.milliseconds.tenths.meaning: A time in milliseconds with one decimal (10 to 100 ms), in an execution profiler row. "ms" is the unit symbol for milliseconds.

profiler.duration.milliseconds.whole.meaning: A time in whole milliseconds (100 ms to one second), in an execution profiler row. "ms" is the unit symbol for milliseconds.

profiler.percent.below-tenth.meaning: A share of the total time that is above zero but less than 0.1 percent, in an execution profiler row.

profiler.percent.whole.meaning: A share of the total time in whole percent (10 percent or more), in an execution profiler row.

placeholders.percent: the share in percent, from 10 to 100

profiler.percent.tenths.meaning: A share of the total time in percent with one decimal (below 10 percent), in an execution profiler row.

profiler.percent.spoken.below-tenth.meaning: A share of the total time read by screen readers: above zero but less than 0.1 percent. Write "percent" as a word.

profiler.percent.spoken.whole.meaning: A share of the total time read by screen readers, in whole percent. Write "percent" as a word.

placeholders.percent: the share in percent, from 10 to 100

profiler.percent.spoken.tenths.meaning: A share of the total time read by screen readers, with one decimal. Write "percent" as a word.

profiler.row.name.meaning: Read by screen readers for one row of the execution profiler: the step, its phase, its time, and its share of the total.

placeholders.step: the step, such as Object placement
placeholders.percent: its share in words, such as 60 percent

profiler.row.work-join.meaning: Joins the lines read by screen readers for one row of the execution profiler (its counts and their explanation) into sentences.

profiler.status.running.waiting.message: Execution profiler: generating, waiting for the engine
profiler.status.running.waiting.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler button while a map is being generated and the map generator (the engine) has not reported its steps yet.

profiler.status.running.waiting-time.message: Execution profiler: generating, waiting for the engine, {seconds, number, ::.00 group-off} seconds
profiler.status.running.waiting-time.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler button while a map is being generated, before the map generator (the engine) reports its steps, with the time so far.

placeholders.seconds: the time in seconds, shown with two decimals

profiler.status.running.steps.message: Execution profiler: generating, {completed} of {total} steps complete
profiler.status.running.steps.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler button while a map is being generated: how many steps are done.

placeholders.total: how many steps the generation has

profiler.status.running.steps-time.message: Execution profiler: generating, {completed} of {total} steps complete, {seconds, number, ::.00 group-off} seconds

placeholders.total: how many steps the generation has
placeholders.seconds: the time in seconds, shown with two decimals

placeholders.seconds: the time in seconds, shown with two decimals

profiler.status.committed.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler button after a map was generated: how long running the RMS script took. Keep RMS (random map script) as written.

placeholders.seconds: the time in seconds, shown with two decimals

profiler.status.unsupported.message: Execution profiler: no measurement for this preview
profiler.status.unsupported.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler button when the shown map has no time measurement.

profiler.status.idle.meaning: Name and tooltip of the execution profiler button (it shows how long each step of generating the map took) when nothing is measured.

profiler.tooltip.running.waiting.meaning: Tooltip of the execution profiler button while a map is being generated and the map generator (the engine) has not reported its steps yet.

profiler.tooltip.running.steps.meaning: Tooltip of the execution profiler button while a map is being generated: how many steps are done.

placeholders.total: how many steps the generation has

profiler.tooltip.cached.meaning: Tooltip of the execution profiler button when the preview reused a map generated earlier (cached), so the time shown was measured then.

profiler.tooltip.committed.meaning: Tooltip of the execution profiler button after a map was generated: it shows how long generating took.

profiler.tooltip.unsupported.meaning: Tooltip of the execution profiler button when the shown map has no time measurement.

profiler.description.message: An approximate local complexity signal from one run on this machine, not a prediction of in-game generation time.
profiler.description.meaning: Read by screen readers for the execution profiler panel: the times are a rough sign of how complex the script is on this computer, not how long the game takes.

profiler.description.cached.message: Cached run: measured when this preview was first generated; the engine did not run again. An approximate local complexity signal from one run on this machine, not a prediction of in-game generation time.
profiler.description.cached.meaning: Read by screen readers for the execution profiler panel when the preview reused a map generated earlier (cached): the times were measured then, and the map generator (the engine) did not run again.

profiler.description.map-test.message: Measured during a map-test run whose samples may run concurrently. An approximate local complexity signal from one run on this machine, not a prediction of in-game generation time.
profiler.description.map-test.meaning: Read by screen readers for the execution profiler panel when the map came from a map test, which may generate several maps at the same time.

profiler.panel.label.meaning: Accessible name of the execution profiler panel, which lists how long each step of generating the map took.

profiler.panel.steps.meaning: Accessible name of the scrolling list of generation steps in the execution profiler panel.

profiler.panel.table.meaning: Accessible name of the table of generation steps in the execution profiler panel, sorted by how long each took.

profiler.panel.empty.message: This preview has no execution-cost measurement.
profiler.panel.empty.meaning: Shown in the execution profiler panel when the shown map has no time measurement.

profiler.chart.label.message: RMS execution time by generation group
profiler.chart.label.meaning: Accessible name of the bar chart in the execution profiler panel: how the time of running the RMS script splits between the phases of generation. Keep RMS (random map script) as written.

profiler.chart.segment.meaning: Tooltip and accessible name of one part of the execution profiler chart: a phase of generation, its time, and its share of the total.

placeholders.group: the phase of generation, such as Land
placeholders.percent: its share of the total, such as 60%

test-results.results.status.passed.meaning: Result word at the start of the Test Results summary: the map test passed (every check held).

test-results.results.status.failed.meaning: Result word at the start of the Test Results summary: the map test failed (some checks did not hold).

test-results.results.status.error.meaning: Result word at the start of the Test Results summary: the map test stopped with an error.

test-results.results.status.stopped.meaning: Result word at the start of the Test Results summary: the user stopped the map test.

placeholders.findings: the findings count, such as "3 findings on 2 seeds"

placeholders.script: the map test's file name, such as Mixed.rmstest

test-results.results.check-headline.meaning: Header of a group of findings in Test Results when the findings have different messages: names the check by its line.

test-results.results.no-findings.passed.meaning: Shown in Test Results when the map test found nothing and every check passed.

placeholders.maps: how many maps the map test generated

placeholders.script: the map test's file name, such as Mixed.rmstest
placeholders.facts: the counts, such as "40 maps · 170 assertions · 3 findings"

placeholders.map: the tested map's file name, such as Demo Valley.rms
placeholders.facts: the counts, such as "40 maps · 170 assertions · 3 findings"

test-results.results.export.meaning: Button in Test Results that saves the results as a report file.

test-results.results.export-tooltip.message: Save these results as a report file. It leaves out your scripts, the generated maps, and full file paths.

test-results.results.list-label.message: {count, plural, one {{count} map test findings} other {{count} map test findings}}

test-results.results.check-source.meaning: Quiet word in the source column of a check's header row in Test Results (a check is an expect or report call of a map test).

test-results.results.show-check-findings.message: Show findings of the check on line {line}

test-results.results.check-findings.message: Findings of the check on line {line}

test-results.results.not-shown.meaning: Beside the Show more button in Test Results: how many findings are still hidden. Starts with a separating dot.

live-test.seed.select-valid-control.message: Select a valid AoE2Control executable first.
live-test.seed.select-valid-control.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the selected AoE2Control file is not usable. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.configure-control.message: Configure AoE2Control to read the current match seed.
live-test.seed.configure-control.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): no AoE2Control is selected. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.connecting.message: AoE2Control is connecting. Try again after the handshake completes.
live-test.seed.connecting.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): AoE2Control is still connecting to the game. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.readback-unavailable.message: Match readback is unavailable. Reconnect AoE2Control and try again.
live-test.seed.readback-unavailable.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): AoE2Control could not read the match. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.replay.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the game shows a recorded game. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.multiplayer.message: Multiplayer match seeds cannot be imported.
live-test.seed.multiplayer.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the game runs a multiplayer match. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.state-changing.message: The match state is changing or unknown. Wait a moment and try again.
live-test.seed.state-changing.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the game is between states. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.no-match.message: Start a supported single-player random-map match first.
live-test.seed.no-match.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): no match is running. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.setup-unreadable.message: The active match setup is unreadable. Reconnect AoE2Control and try again.
live-test.seed.setup-unreadable.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the running match's setup could not be read. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.not-random-map.message: The active match is not a supported Random Map match.
live-test.seed.not-random-map.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the running match is not a Random Map game (the game mode name: use the game's official wording). AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.seed-unreadable.message: The active match seed is unreadable. Reconnect AoE2Control and try again.
live-test.seed.seed-unreadable.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): the running match's seed could not be read. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.busy.message: An AoE2Control operation is already in progress.
live-test.seed.busy.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): another AoE2Control action is running. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.seed.not-returned.message: AoE2Control did not return the match seed.
live-test.seed.not-returned.meaning: Why the running match's seed can't be read into the run settings now (tooltip of the unavailable seed import, and the Output note after a failed import): AoE2Control answered without a seed. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.control.missing.message: The selected executable moved or was removed.
live-test.control.missing.meaning: The run menu's AoE2Control line when the selected AoE2Control file is gone. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.control.changed.message: The selected executable changed. Select it again to trust the new file.
live-test.control.changed.meaning: The run menu's AoE2Control line when the selected AoE2Control file changed since it was selected. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

live-test.control.invalid.message: The selected file is not a valid public AoE2Control executable.
live-test.control.invalid.meaning: The run menu's AoE2Control line when the selected file is not AoE2Control. AoE2Control is a product name and stays as written.

workspace.format.save-skipped.meaning: Output headline: Format on Save did not format the file, which was saved unformatted. The cause line says why.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.format.save-cancelled.meaning: Output headline: the save did not happen because formatting the file before saving could not finish. The cause line says why.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.format.read-only.message: {name} is read-only and was not formatted
workspace.format.read-only.meaning: Output headline after Format Document on a file that cannot be changed (such as a game file opened for reading).

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.format.unchanged.meaning: Output headline after Format Document when formatting changed nothing.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.format.not-formatted.meaning: Output headline after Format Document when the formatter refused or failed. The cause line says why.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.format.reason.timeout.message: The formatter did not finish in time.
workspace.format.reason.timeout.meaning: Cause sentence under a formatting headline: the formatter took too long and was stopped.

workspace.format.reason.not-proven.meaning: Cause sentence under a formatting headline when the formatter gave no reason: it could not prove the formatted script means the same as the original, so it kept the original.

workspace.format.reason.stale.meaning: Cause sentence under 'Save cancelled' when the formatter gave no reason: the text changed while it was being formatted for the save.

workspace.files.deleted-outside.meaning: Output headline: another program deleted a file open in the editor. AoE2RMSIDE (the product name) stays as written.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.files.deleted-outside.cause.message: Its text stays open in the editor.
workspace.files.deleted-outside.cause.meaning: Cause sentence under the headline that a file was deleted outside AoE2RMSIDE: the editor keeps its text as unsaved work.

workspace.files.reloaded.message: Reloaded {name} after it changed on disk
workspace.files.reloaded.meaning: Output headline: another program changed an open file, and the editor now shows the new text from disk.

placeholders.name: the file name, such as Arabia.rms

workspace.recovery.restored.message: Recovered {count, plural, one {{count} unsaved buffer} other {{count} unsaved buffers}} from the previous session
workspace.recovery.restored.meaning: Output headline at startup: unsaved editor text from the last run (which ended without saving) was restored into tabs. A buffer is the unsaved text of one tab.

placeholders.count: how many tabs of unsaved text were restored

workspace.recovery.restored.cause.meaning: Cause sentence under the recovered-work headline: the files on disk still hold their last saved text.

workspace.failed.save.message: The file could not be saved
workspace.failed.save.meaning: Output headline when saving a file failed and no more specific message applies.

workspace.failed.open-file.message: The file could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-file.meaning: Output headline when opening a file failed and no more specific message applies.

workspace.failed.open-folder.message: The folder could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-folder.meaning: Output headline when opening a folder in the Explorer failed and no more specific message applies.

workspace.failed.open-recent.message: The recent item could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-recent.meaning: Output headline when a file or folder chosen from File → Open Recent could not be opened.

workspace.failed.open-requested.message: The requested items could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-requested.meaning: Output headline when files or folders Windows asked the app to open (a double-clicked file, an Explorer action, the command line) could not be opened.

workspace.failed.open-dropped.message: The dropped items could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-dropped.meaning: Output headline when files dragged onto the window could not be opened.

workspace.failed.open-map-item-source.message: The script behind this map item could not be opened
workspace.failed.open-map-item-source.meaning: Output headline when the script line that placed an item selected in the map preview could not be opened in the editor.

workspace.failed.create.message: The item could not be created
workspace.failed.create.meaning: Output headline when creating a file or folder in the Explorer failed.

workspace.failed.rename.message: The item could not be renamed
workspace.failed.rename.meaning: Output headline when renaming a file or folder in the Explorer failed.

workspace.failed.delete.message: The item could not be deleted
workspace.failed.delete.meaning: Output headline when deleting a file or folder in the Explorer failed.

workspace.failed.restore-session.message: The previous session could not be restored
workspace.failed.restore-session.meaning: Output headline at startup when the tabs, folder, and unsaved work of the last run could not be restored.

workspace.failed.back-up.message: Unsaved work could not be backed up
workspace.failed.back-up.meaning: Output headline when the automatic background copy of unsaved editor text (used to recover it after a crash) could not be written.

message.RMS4009.cause.acts.message: The game acts on {word} after it, because only text between /* and */ written apart is skipped.
message.RMS4009.cause.acts.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4009 when the game acts on a word after // or ; in another way (a random number, a defined name whose value it reads).

placeholders.word: the word as written, such as rnd(1,5)

message.RMS4009.cause.dispatches.message: The game runs the defined name {name} after it as the command {command}, because only text between /* and */ written apart is skipped.
message.RMS4009.cause.dispatches.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4009 when a defined name after // or ; stands where a command can stand, so the game runs the command its value names.

placeholders.name: the defined name as written, such as ROAD
placeholders.command: the command the name's value runs, such as right_border

message.RMS4009.cause.runs.message: The game runs {command} after it, because only text between /* and */ written apart is skipped.
message.RMS4009.cause.runs.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4009 when the game runs a command written after // or ; on the same line.

placeholders.command: the command as written, such as set_tight_grouping

message.RMS4009.cause.skipped.message: The game skips the words after it only because none of them is a command or a defined name it acts on here; /* and */ written apart keep them skipped.
message.RMS4009.cause.skipped.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4009 as a hint, when the game skips every word after // or ; on the line.

message.RMS4010.headline.meaning: Headline of the RMS lint finding RMS4010 (a plain number written where the game reads a name, so it ignores the command), shown in Problems and the editor.

message.RMS4010.headline.named.meaning: Headline of the RMS lint finding RMS4010, shown in Problems and the editor.

placeholders.command: the RMS command as written, such as create_object or effect_amount

message.RMS4010.cause.message: A plain number stands where the game reads a name, and it only finds defined names there.
message.RMS4010.cause.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4010, shown in Problems and the editor.

message.RMS4010.cause.named.message: {number} is a plain number where the game reads a name, and it only finds defined names there.
message.RMS4010.cause.named.meaning: Cause sentence of the RMS lint finding RMS4010 naming the number, shown in Problems and the editor.

placeholders.number: the number as written, such as 66

message.RMS4010.action.message: Define the number with #const and use the name
message.RMS4010.action.meaning: Next-step label of the RMS lint finding RMS4010, shown in Problems and the editor.

editor-assistance.limited.capacity.message: Use a smaller source folder or close some source tabs, then retry.
editor-assistance.limited.capacity.meaning: Capacity-only editor recovery action for a bounded inventory-discovery or diagnostic-queue refusal. A smaller folder reduces closed-source lookup work; fewer tabs can reduce queued editor diagnostics. Never used for missing or unauthorized file errors.

editor-assistance.limited.diagnostic-que.message: Some editor diagnostics were skipped because the update queue is full.
editor-assistance.limited.diagnostic-que.meaning: Cause of the bounded main diagnostic-publication queue refusing an update. The skipped diagnostics are not presented as complete; the app does not enter an automatic republish loop.

editor-assistance.limited.headline.meaning: Main-owned warning when the current editor inventory or diagnostic admission refuses assistance. Generation remains independent. Stale source facts are refused, never reused.

editor-assistance.limited.retry.message: Check Details for the affected sources, then try again.
editor-assistance.limited.retry.meaning: Neutral recovery action for changed, missing or unauthorized editor sources, or another non-capacity refusal. Details names the Output row's disclosure containing the precise original error. Do not imply deleting sources or switching to a smaller folder is necessary.

editor-assistance.limited.sources.message: Some editor checks could not use the current source files.
editor-assistance.limited.sources.meaning: Cause when current authorized closed RMS/XS sources or strict source context cannot be validated for editor assistance. Some same-current open-document assistance remains available. This does not say a preview or map test failed.

file-actions.included-files.budget.depth.meaning: Short budget name for at most64 relative path components from an authorized resolution root.

file-actions.included-files.budget.direc.meaning: Short budget name for65536 visited filesystem names during needed directory probes. Entries includes files and subdirectories, even unrelated/rejected names in that required directory.

file-actions.included-files.budget.metad.meaning: Short budget name inserted into the include discovery limit sentence. One shared2MiB bound for retained include keys, candidate paths, directory names and probe identity metadata; counts bytes, not source-file bodies.

file-actions.included-files.budget.paths.meaning: Short budget name inserted into the include discovery limit sentence. Counts distinct include request keys or resolver candidate probe paths; limit4096 for either separate collection.

file-actions.included-files.changed.message: Sources changed while includes were being checked. Run again.
file-actions.included-files.changed.meaning: A graph/entry/open buffer/root/native-process change invalidated in-flight include preparation or current graph proof. No cached map is claimed current.

file-actions.included-files.discovery-li.message: Include discovery exceeded the {budget} limit for {scope}: {used, number, integer} used; limit {maximum, number, integer}.
file-actions.included-files.discovery-li.meaning: Cause for a bounded dependency discovery refusal in main. budget is another translated short label, scope is a bounded authored include path or local folder name, used and maximum are integer counts. This concerns names and lookup work, not the selected source bodies.

placeholders.budget: the translated short budget label, such as include paths or directory entries
placeholders.scope: the local include path or folder being checked, bounded to 512 characters and not translated
placeholders.used: the integer amount used in the unit named by budget, formatted for the interface locale
placeholders.maximum: the integer limit in the same unit, formatted for the interface locale

file-actions.included-files.discovery-re.message: Use a smaller include folder or reduce the required includes.
file-actions.included-files.discovery-re.meaning: Recovery action following a dependency discovery names/path/metadata/depth budget refusal. Include means an RMS dependency file, not a UI inclusion action.

file-actions.map-test-sources.failed.message: The sources for the map test could not be prepared
file-actions.map-test-sources.failed.meaning: Main-owned Output warning headline when a bounded multi-map source batch cannot be prepared before execution. Independent of native RMS/map-test diagnostics, which remain English.

file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.byte.message: The map test exceeds the source data limit of {limit, number, integer} MiB. Run fewer maps in one test.
file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.byte.meaning: Cause of a main-owned map-test input refusal before execution. Limits total source-file content across all map graphs, including repeated shared dependencies. MiB is the binary size unit; one MiB is 1048576 bytes.

placeholders.limit: integer maximum source-body size in MiB, formatted in the interface locale; currently 16, not a raw byte count

file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.maps.message: The map test exceeds the limit of {limit, number, integer} maps. Run fewer maps in one test.
file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.maps.meaning: Cause of a main-owned map-test input refusal before execution. Counts distinct RMS map roots in one test, including its pinned map. This is not the number of generated samples or seeds.

placeholders.limit: integer maximum map-root count, formatted in the interface locale; currently 64

file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.meta.message: The map test exceeds the source metadata limit of {limit, number, integer} MiB. Run fewer maps in one test.
file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.meta.meaning: Cause of a main-owned map-test input refusal before execution. Metadata includes source paths, identifiers, roots, definitions and main's lookup witnesses across the batch, not source-file contents. MiB is the binary size unit.

placeholders.limit: integer maximum metadata size in MiB, formatted in the interface locale; currently 2, not a raw byte count

file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.reco.message: The map test exceeds the limit of {limit, number, integer} source records. Run fewer maps in one test.
file-actions.map-test-sources.limit.reco.meaning: Cause of a main-owned map-test input refusal before execution. Source records are RMS/XS source files carried in each map's dependency graph; a shared file counts again when included by another map because it is sent again.

placeholders.limit: integer maximum serialized source-record count, formatted in the interface locale; currently 4096

file-actions.included-files.required-lim.message: {scope} exceeds the per-file limit of {limit, number, integer} MiB.
file-actions.included-files.required-lim.meaning: Required RMS/XS source data is refused before preparation because one entry or dependency exceeds the encoded per-file capacity. This includes dirty buffers and preserves the original encoding, BOM and newline bytes. scope is the bounded local filename/path, never translated.

placeholders.scope: the local filename/path bounded to 512 characters, not translated
placeholders.limit: the exact byte limit divided by 1,048,576 to express MiB; the fixed limits are whole MiB, formatted for the interface locale

file-actions.included-files.required-lim.message: Required source files exceed the total limit of {limit, number, integer} MiB.
file-actions.included-files.required-lim.meaning: The current generation graph exceeds its total encoded source-body capacity, counting the entry plus all conservatively required RMS and XS dependency candidates. Unrelated editor files are outside this generation bound.

placeholders.limit: the exact byte limit divided by 1,048,576 to express MiB; the fixed limits are whole MiB, formatted for the interface locale

file-actions.included-files.required-lim.message: Required source files exceed the limit of {limit, number, integer} files.
file-actions.included-files.required-lim.meaning: The current generation graph exceeds its retained source-record count, including the entry and RMS/XS dependencies. Distinct candidate paths count; repeated references to the same retained source do not.

placeholders.limit: the integer source-record limit, formatted for the interface locale

file-actions.included-files.required-lim.message: Required source information exceeds the metadata limit of {limit, number, integer} MiB.
file-actions.included-files.required-lim.meaning: Required source identities, paths, root/context and selected vocabulary metadata cannot fit the shared retained metadata bound. Selected source metadata shares the same limit with dependency discovery names and witnesses; this cause identifies a required-information charge, not file body bytes.

placeholders.limit: the exact byte limit divided by 1,048,576 to express MiB; the fixed limits are whole MiB, formatted for the interface locale

file-actions.included-files.required-lim.message: Reduce the required source data, then run again.
file-actions.included-files.required-lim.meaning: Recovery after a required-generation-source file, total body, record-count or metadata capacity refusal. Reduce the dependencies or their data before running again. The previous map may remain visible but is not claimed current.

release-check.newer.headline.meaning: Output note shown when the app starts and a newer AoE2RMSIDE release is published on GitHub. AoE2RMSIDE is the product name and stays as written.

placeholders.version: the newer release's version, such as 1.0.0

release-check.newer.cause.meaning: Names the version the user runs, below the note about the newer release.

placeholders.current: the version the user runs, such as 0.9.1-preview.5

release-check.newer.action.meaning: Link in the newer-release note: opens the AoE2RMSIDE releases page on GitHub in the browser, where the user downloads the new version. The app downloads and installs nothing itself.
